A: SPAs may use location.hash for anchors (e.g. #section-id). If you use multiple prefixes like #folder- and #folderdir-, parse longest match first—naive startsWith('folder-') breaks on substrings. Preserve hashes across history.replaceState cleanup.

Also asked as: hash deep links · overlapping hash prefixes

chunks.title: How do I sign and broadcast a transaction?
chunks.text:
## Q: How do I sign and broadcast a transaction?

A: Use SIGN_TRANSACTION for a Hub-signed transaction, then broadcast via REST /transactions/process. Keep signing behind an explicit user action and never handle seed phrases. Verify the exact payload shape for your Core version.

Also asked as: SIGN_TRANSACTION · broadcast transaction · transactions/process

chunks.title: How do group actions work?
chunks.text:
## Q: How do group actions work?

A: LIST_GROUPS, JOIN_GROUP, and GET_GROUPS_WITH_MEMBER manage membership. JOIN_GROUP requires approval. Use groups with ENCRYPT_QORTAL_GROUP_DATA when sharing private payloads among members. Feature-detect and handle cancel.

Also asked as: LIST_GROUPS · JOIN_GROUP · group membership

chunks.title: Why is SEARCH_TRANSACTIONS message often missing?
chunks.text:
## Q: Why is SEARCH_TRANSACTIONS message often missing?

A: Payment matching via SEARCH_TRANSACTIONS often lacks a reliable message field. Match by reference, type, amounts (1e8 scale), and parties instead of free-text memo. Design payment protocols that do not depend on message alone.

Also asked as: SEARCH_TRANSACTIONS · payment matching · transaction message missing

chunks.title: What are Hub list actions?
chunks.text:
## Q: What are Hub list actions?

A: GET_LIST_ITEMS, ADD_LIST_ITEMS, and DELETE_LIST_ITEM manage per-user lists in Hub UI state—not global QDN. Use for bookmarks/favorites local to the user. Persist shared data on QDN JSON/FILE instead of lists when others must read it.

Also asked as: GET_LIST_ITEMS · ADD_LIST_ITEMS · hub lists

chunks.title: How do I test auth edge cases?
chunks.text:
## Q: How do I test auth edge cases?

A: Cover: user cancels GET_USER_ACCOUNT; wallet with zero names; nested iframe without relay; opening index.html outside Hub (preview mode). Ensure publish buttons stay disabled without a name and errors are human-readable.

Also asked as: test auth cancel · no name wallet test

chunks.title: What is the difference between QDN search mode ALL and LATEST?
chunks.text:
## Q: What is the difference between QDN search mode ALL and LATEST?

A: REST QDN search modes mode=ALL vs mode=LATEST change whether you see historical publishes or only latest per coordinate. Wrong mode causes duplicates or wrong counts. Prefer LATEST for current app state unless you need history.

Also asked as: mode=ALL · mode=LATEST · qdn search mode

chunks.title: Where is the REST API documentation?
chunks.text:
## Q: Where is the REST API documentation?

A: Use https://api.qortal.org/api-documentation/ for node REST fields. Cross-check field names when debugging bridge vs REST mismatches. For qortalRequest actions, prefer https://qortal.dev/docs/q-apps and Core Q-Apps.md.

Also asked as: api.qortal.org · rest docs qortal

chunks.title: What GitHub repos should Q-App developers study?
chunks.text:
## Q: What GitHub repos should Q-App developers study?

A: Qortal/qortal (Core, Q-Apps.md, q-apps.js), Qortal/Qortal-Hub, optional Qortal/qapp-core helpers, and reference apps q-mail, q-share, q-tube, q-shop. Community projects also live on https://gitea.qortal.link.

Also asked as: q-app github repos · qapp-core · gitea.qortal.link

chunks.title: How do I feature-detect optional publish batching?
chunks.text:
## Q: How do I feature-detect optional publish batching?

A: Try PUBLISH_MULTIPLE_QDN_RESOURCES inside try/catch; on failure fall back to sequential PUBLISH_QDN_RESOURCE with clear progress. Do not invent parameters—check qortal.dev for the user's version.

Also asked as: feature detect batch publish

chunks.title: What if payment succeeded but notification failed?
chunks.text:
## Q: What if payment succeeded but notification failed?

A: Treat payment and notification as separate steps. Persist local state that payment confirmed (tx signature/reference) even if a follow-up QDN publish or chat notify fails, then retry notify without charging again.

Also asked as: payment notify failed · separate payment steps

chunks.title: Why are case-sensitive paths important in zips?
chunks.text:
## Q: Why are case-sensitive paths important in zips?

A: QDN/Hub serving is case-sensitive. Mismatched Asset vs asset paths work on some desktop FS previews and fail in Hub. Prefer lowercase [a-z0-9._-] filenames and matching import paths from the bundler.

Also asked as: case-sensitive paths · zip path case

chunks.title: How do I load demo JSON after connect in a skeleton app?
chunks.text:
## Q: How do I load demo JSON after connect in a skeleton app?

A: After Connect obtains a primary name, PUBLISH_QDN_RESOURCE a small JSON with identifier myapp_demo_<timestamp> and data64 from b64Utf8, then FETCH_QDN_RESOURCE the same coordinates and display the result. Disable the load/publish button until a name exists.

Also asked as: skeleton publish fetch · demo json q-app

chunks.title: How do Hub themes affect my Q-App UI?
chunks.text:
## Q: How do Hub themes affect my Q-App UI?

A: Read window._qdnTheme ("light"|"dark") and style accordingly so the app matches Hub chrome. Re-check on visibility changes if Hub can toggle theme while open. Avoid assuming dark mode defaults.

Also asked as: hub theme q-app · match hub light dark

chunks.title: How do I keep Hub copy-link accurate for WEBSITE subpages?
chunks.text:
## Q: How do I keep Hub copy-link accurate for WEBSITE subpages?

A: On each route change, call QDN_RESOURCE_DISPLAYED with service WEBSITE, name, and path. Optionally update canonical qortal://WEBSITE/<name>/<slug>. Without this, copy-link may point only at the site root.

Also asked as: copy-link subpath · website path displayed

chunks.title: What is GET_ACCOUNT_DATA?
chunks.text:
## Q: What is GET_ACCOUNT_DATA?

A: GET_ACCOUNT_DATA returns the account record for an address (read-only, typically no approval). Use it for public account fields after you know an address from GET_USER_ACCOUNT or a name lookup.

Also asked as: GET_ACCOUNT_DATA · account record

chunks.title: What is GET_BALANCE used for?
chunks.text:
## Q: What is GET_BALANCE used for?

A: GET_BALANCE reads a balance for an address without implying the logged-in wallet session. For the user's wallet-specific balance UI, also consider approval-gated wallet balance actions on your Hub version. Remember 1e8 scaling for QORT display.

Also asked as: GET_BALANCE · read balance q-app

chunks.title: What chain helpers exist via qortalRequest?
chunks.text:
## Q: What chain helpers exist via qortalRequest?

A: Common helpers include FETCH_BLOCK, FETCH_BLOCK_RANGE, GET_BLOCK_HEIGHT, GET_PRICE, DEPLOY_AT, GET_AT, GET_AT_DATA, LIST_ATS, and day summary reads. Verify names/params for your Core; wrap in try/catch and prefer relative REST fetch for simple public chain reads.

Also asked as: FETCH_BLOCK · GET_BLOCK_HEIGHT · DEPLOY_AT · GET_AT

chunks.title: How do I link to a WEBSITE sub-page?
chunks.text:
## Q: How do I link to a WEBSITE sub-page?

A: Use qortal://WEBSITE/MySite/gallery (service/name/path). Ensure the WEBSITE zip actually contains that path or APP-style SPA fallback will not apply—WEBSITE 404s missing files. Sync Hub chrome with QDN_RESOURCE_DISPLAYED.

Also asked as: website subpage link · qortal website path

chunks.title: What is local preview URL for an APP?
chunks.text:
## Q: What is local preview URL for an APP?

A: When Core supports it: http://localhost:12391/render/APP/<Name>?preview=true (varies by version). Still prefer Hub Preview for realistic bridge behavior. Confirm assets load under the render path.

Also asked as: local preview render · preview=true url

chunks.title: How do I use GET_QDN_RESOURCE_STATUS before playing video?
chunks.text:
## Q: How do I use GET_QDN_RESOURCE_STATUS before playing video?

A: Poll or await GET_QDN_RESOURCE_STATUS until READY (and acceptable percent loaded) before setting video src or fetching large blobs. Show progress UI; cancel cleanly on navigation away.

Also asked as: video ready status · wait for media READY

chunks.title: How do I get a URL for an arbitrary resource path?
chunks.text:
## Q: How do I get a URL for an arbitrary resource path?

A: Prefer GET_QDN_RESOURCE_URL over string-concatenating /arbitrary/... yourself. For multi-file resources include the filepath Hub expects. Append ?attachment=true on mobile when triggering native download listeners.

Also asked as: arbitrary resource url · filepath url

chunks.title: What is OPEN_NEW_TAB used for?
chunks.text:
## Q: What is OPEN_NEW_TAB used for?

A: OPEN_NEW_TAB opens a new Hub tab with a URL or qortal:// link. Use it for cross-app navigation while staying inside Hub. Prefer it over external browser windows for QDN targets.

Also asked as: OPEN_NEW_TAB · new hub tab

chunks.title: How does SET_TAB postMessage work?
chunks.text:
## Q: How does SET_TAB postMessage work?

A: Post a message like { action: 'SET_TAB', requestedHandler: 'UI', payload: { service, name, identifier?, path? } } to switch Hub tabs to a QDN resource. Feature-detect Hub support and fall back to LINK_TO_QDN_RESOURCE or OPEN_NEW_TAB.

Also asked as: SET_TAB postMessage · hub tab switch

chunks.title: How should category and tags be used on resources?
chunks.text:
## Q: How should category and tags be used on resources?

A: Set category/tags in publish metadata when supported, and read them via GET_QDN_RESOURCE_METADATA for filtering UIs. Keep tags short and consistent within your app. Do not trust tags for security decisions—validate payload bodies.

Also asked as: resource category tags · metadata tags

chunks.title: What does latest publish wins mean for identifiers?
chunks.text:
## Q: What does latest publish wins mean for identifiers?

A: Updating the same name+service+identifier overwrites prior content for readers fetching latest. To keep history, use new identifiers or version suffixes and point the index at the current id. Design for immutability when audits matter.

Also asked as: immutable identifiers · version suffix identifiers

chunks.title: How do I debug bridge vs REST field mismatches?
chunks.text:
## Q: How do I debug bridge vs REST field mismatches?

A: Compare qortalRequest responses with the same data from relative fetch against api.qortal.org field names. Log raw payloads in Preview. Prefer bridge for wallet-bound ops and REST/fetch for anonymous public reads.

Also asked as: bridge vs rest · debug field names

chunks.title: What is GET_USER_WALLET vs GET_USER_ACCOUNT?
chunks.text:
## Q: What is GET_USER_WALLET vs GET_USER_ACCOUNT?

A: GET_USER_ACCOUNT returns address/publicKey for identity. GET_USER_WALLET / GET_USER_WALLET_INFO are approval-gated wallet details on some Hubs—use only when needed and verify fields for your version. Prefer the least-privileged action.

Also asked as: GET_USER_WALLET · GET_USER_WALLET_INFO

chunks.title: How do I display QORT prices?
chunks.text:
## Q: How do I display QORT prices?

A: Call GET_PRICE (read-only) and divide integer amounts by 1e8 for human QORT. Cache briefly to avoid spamming; handle missing market data. Confirm units before using prices in SEND_COIN UX copy.

Also asked as: GET_PRICE · display qort price

chunks.title: What is SEARCH_NAMES for?
chunks.text:
## Q: What is SEARCH_NAMES for?

A: SEARCH_NAMES finds registered names (read-only). Use it for typeahead when linking to publishers. After picking a name, fetch resources with LIST/SEARCH QDN APIs and validate payloads.

Also asked as: SEARCH_NAMES · name search

chunks.title: How should error messages be written for users?
chunks.text:
## Q: How should error messages be written for users?

A: Map bridge errors to short actions: open in Hub, connect wallet, register a name, approve the popup, reduce payload size, or retry after publish delay. Avoid dumping raw stacks. Distinguish cancel from failure.

Also asked as: user facing errors · q-app error ux

chunks.title: How do I keep Q-App builds deterministic for republish?
chunks.text:
## Q: How do I keep Q-App builds deterministic for republish?

A: Pin dependency versions, rebuild clean dist/, zip contents only, and bump manifest version. After publish, verify GET_QDN_RESOURCE_PROPERTIES size/hash expectations. Stale hashed assets in an old zip cause eternal Loading.

Also asked as: deterministic build zip · republish clean build

chunks.title: What crossorigin script issue can grey-screen an app?
chunks.text:
## Q: What crossorigin script issue can grey-screen an app?

A: Some Hub builds fail loading scripts marked crossorigin, leaving a blank/Loading UI even when files exist. If assets 200 but JS never runs, try removing crossorigin from script tags, rebuild, and re-zip.

Also asked as: crossorigin script hub · script load fail

chunks.title: How do I design identifier namespaces for encrypted mail-like apps?
chunks.text:
## Q: How do I design identifier namespaces for encrypted mail-like apps?

A: Use public JSON indexes under myapp_pub_* and ciphertext under myapp_priv_* (or private services). ENCRYPT_DATA with recipient publicKeys; DECRYPT_DATA with counterparty publicKey. Never put secrets in public JSON.

Also asked as: encrypted mail identifiers · public vs private namespace

chunks.title: How do I use polls safely in a Q-App?
chunks.text:
## Q: How do I use polls safely in a Q-App?

A: Ensure pollName uniqueness, pass pollOptions as an array of option objects, confirm copy before CREATE_POLL/VOTE_ON_POLL approvals, and handle cancel. Do not encode critical funds movement only in poll text—use SEND_COIN for payments.

Also asked as: polls best practices · pollName unique

chunks.title: How do I report resource display to Hub for APP routes?
chunks.text:
## Q: How do I report resource display to Hub for APP routes?

A: Use QDN_RESOURCE_DISPLAYED with service APP, name, and path when your in-app route should appear in Hub chrome/copy-link. Keep path aligned with what you would put in a qortal:// link.

Also asked as: QDN_RESOURCE_DISPLAYED APP · app route copy link

chunks.title: What is the teaching-default artifact for small tools?
chunks.text:
## Q: What is the teaching-default artifact for small tools?

A: Default to a single-file HTML Q-App for small tools, and Vite + flat zip for production SPAs. Single-file simplifies packaging (still may zip one html); SPAs need careful relative asset paths and SPA service APP.

Also asked as: single-file html q-app · default artifact

chunks.title: What METADATA fields are commonly useful in galleries?
chunks.text:
## Q: What METADATA fields are commonly useful in galleries?

A: Title, tags, category from GET_QDN_RESOURCE_METADATA plus filename/mimeType/size from PROPERTIES and a THUMBNAIL URL. Lazy-load full FETCH only on open. Validate strings before rendering into HTML.

Also asked as: gallery metadata fields · lazy load resource

chunks.title: What is the difference between gateway context and full Hub?
chunks.text:
## Q: What is the difference between gateway context and full Hub?

A: window._qdnContext may be "gateway" vs fuller Hub environments. Some privileged behaviors differ; always feature-detect qortalRequest and degrade. Theme still via _qdnTheme. Test both if you support public gateways.

Also asked as: _qdnContext gateway · gateway vs hub

chunks.title: What FILE size strategy should apps use?
chunks.text:
## Q: What FILE size strategy should apps use?

A: Prefer one FILE when under comfortable Hub timeouts; for larger binaries, chunk into parts with a JSON index and bounded parallel fetches. Probe STATUS before heavy FETCH. Show clear size warnings before user-approved publish.

Also asked as: large file strategy · file size timeouts

chunks.title: How do I fetch account names with pagination?
chunks.text:
## Q: How do I fetch account names with pagination?

A: Pass limit and offset to GET_ACCOUNT_NAMES and loop until a short page returns. Most users have few names—still code defensively. Cache after Connect for the session unless the user refreshes names.

Also asked as: GET_ACCOUNT_NAMES pagination · limit offset names

chunks.title: How do relative asset paths interact with deep links?
chunks.text:
## Q: How do relative asset paths interact with deep links?

A: Deep links into /render/APP/Name/some/route still need assets resolved from the app root, not the deep path. Relative ./assets from a nested route can break—use root-correct relative URLs from the bundler base or Hub trailing-slash strategies.

Also asked as: deep link assets · nested route asset paths

chunks.title: How do I use DOCUMENT vs FILE for text?
chunks.text:
## Q: How do I use DOCUMENT vs FILE for text?

A: DOCUMENT suits larger text/JSON documents; FILE is generic binary/download oriented. If clients should edit structured text in-app, DOCUMENT (or JSON when tiny) is clearer; if users download opaque blobs, FILE fits. Either way validate size and mime.

Also asked as: DOCUMENT vs FILE · text on qdn

chunks.title: What Hub UI actions help multi-page sites?
chunks.text:
## Q: What Hub UI actions help multi-page sites?

A: QDN_RESOURCE_DISPLAYED keeps copy-link aligned; OPEN_NEW_TAB/LINK_TO_QDN_RESOURCE opens peers; SET_TAB switches tabs; SET_TAB_NOTIFICATIONS badges unread. Combine with real WEBSITE file paths or APP SPA fallback appropriately.

Also asked as: hub ui actions website · multi-page hub integration

chunks.title: How do I safely mock data in preview mode?
chunks.text:
## Q: How do I safely mock data in preview mode?

A: When the bridge is missing, serve local fixture JSON for reads and disable Publish/Pay buttons. Label the UI Preview. Never mark a mock payment as success. The same code paths should call qr() in Hub.

Also asked as: mock preview data · fixtures without hub

chunks.title: What is the end-to-end path for a WEBSITE visitor link?
chunks.text:
## Q: What is the end-to-end path for a WEBSITE visitor link?

A: Publisher builds static files → Hub publishes service WEBSITE under owned name → visitors open qortal://WEBSITE/<Name>/path. Missing files 404. For interactive wallet features on every page, consider APP instead.

Also asked as: website visitor path · end to end website

chunks.title: What REST mode mistake causes duplicate resources in UI?
chunks.text:
## Q: What REST mode mistake causes duplicate resources in UI?

A: Using mode=ALL when you meant LATEST lists historical publishes as separate rows. Prefer LATEST for current catalogs, or dedupe by name+service+identifier yourself if you need ALL for history UIs.

Also asked as: duplicate resources search mode · ALL vs LATEST duplicates

chunks.title: How do I implement bounded concurrency in JS?
chunks.text:
## Q: How do I implement bounded concurrency in JS?

A: Keep a queue of identifiers and N workers: while queue length, worker shifts an id, await FETCH_QDN_RESOURCE, push result, repeat. Avoid awaiting Promise.all on the entire list. Surface partial errors per id.

Also asked as: worker pool fetch · bounded concurrency code

chunks.title: What should happen when parent.qortalRequest is only a stub?
chunks.text:
## Q: What should happen when parent.qortalRequest is only a stub?

A: If parent === top and the stub cannot reach Hub, wallet calls fail—tell the user to open the app from Hub or a real Hub tab. Implement a message relay only when you control the parent embedder.

Also asked as: stub qortalRequest · parent top stub

chunks.title: What UI pattern fits Hub-embedded Q-Apps?
chunks.text:
## Q: What UI pattern fits Hub-embedded Q-Apps?

A: One primary Connect CTA, clear publish/pay confirmations, theme via _qdnTheme, large tap targets, and progressive loading with STATUS for media. Avoid assuming desktop hover. Keep critical actions gesture-gated.

Also asked as: hub embedded ui pattern · q-app ux pattern

chunks.title: What FILE identifier pattern do blog/mail apps use?
chunks.text:
## Q: What FILE identifier pattern do blog/mail apps use?

A: File attachments in blog/mail-style apps often use FILE with identifiers like qfile_…. Follow the host app's documented prefix so other clients can find attachments. Validate mime/size from GET_QDN_RESOURCE_PROPERTIES before rendering.

Also asked as: qfile identifier · file attachment identifier

chunks.title: What is NAVIGATION_HISTORY for?
chunks.text:
## Q: What is NAVIGATION_HISTORY for?

A: NAVIGATION_HISTORY integrates back/forward with Hub (availability is Hub-dependent). Use it when your SPA should participate in Hub navigation chrome. Always feature-detect and provide in-app back affordances as fallback.

Also asked as: NAVIGATION_HISTORY · hub back forward

chunks.title: What is qapp-core?
chunks.text:
## Q: What is qapp-core?

A: Qortal/qapp-core is an optional npm helper library for Q-App development. It can wrap common bridge patterns, but you should still understand raw qortalRequest and verify actions against your Hub/Core version.

Also asked as: qapp-core npm · qortal qapp-core

chunks.title: Should Connect buttons meet mobile touch targets?
chunks.text:
## Q: Should Connect buttons meet mobile touch targets?

A: Yes. Use adequate tap targets (e.g. min-height ~44px) for Connect, Publish, and payment buttons. Mobile Hub and Qortal Go are primary surfaces—avoid hover-only UX and tiny icon-only critical actions.

Also asked as: mobile touch targets · button size q-app

chunks.title: What is GIF_REPOSITORY?
chunks.text:
## Q: What is GIF_REPOSITORY?

A: GIF_REPOSITORY is a multi-file QDN service type (like APP/WEBSITE) requiring filepath on fetch. Use it for gif packs rather than APP UI. Confirm size limits and publish path via Hub for your Core version.

Also asked as: GIF_REPOSITORY · gif repository service

chunks.title: Can I use STORE or PRODUCT services?
chunks.text:
## Q: Can I use STORE or PRODUCT services?

A: Q-Shop-style apps use STORE/PRODUCT services plus payment actions. Follow Q-Shop conventions for identifiers and JSON schemas rather than inventing incompatible shapes if you want ecosystem interoperability. Always validate foreign product JSON.

Also asked as: STORE service · PRODUCT service · q-shop services

chunks.title: How do identifiers work with MAIL or BLOG_POST?
chunks.text:
## Q: How do identifiers work with MAIL or BLOG_POST?

A: Follow each ecosystem app's documented identifier schemes (Q-Mail, Q-Blog) so other clients interoperate. Prefix your own extensions carefully and never overwrite foreign coordinates. Validate payload schemas from those apps' repos.

Also asked as: mail identifiers · blog_post identifiers

chunks.title: What friends/profile list actions exist?
chunks.text:
## Q: What friends/profile list actions exist?

A: Hub builds may expose GET_FRIENDS_LIST, SET_PROFILE_DATA, and list item APIs—often approval-gated. Verify against your version's q-apps docs before relying on them. Store cross-user public profile data on QDN when other apps must read it.

Also asked as: GET_FRIENDS_LIST · SET_PROFILE_DATA

chunks.title: What is SEND_CHAT_MESSAGE used for?
chunks.text:
## Q: What is SEND_CHAT_MESSAGE used for?

A: SEND_CHAT_MESSAGE (group) sends chat with user approval on supported Hubs. Do not use it as a reliable payment receipt channel. Confirm group context and permissions; handle cancel and rate limits.

Also asked as: SEND_CHAT_MESSAGE · group chat message

chunks.title: What notifications permission actions exist?
chunks.text:
## Q: What notifications permission actions exist?

A: Some Hub versions expose notifications permission actions alongside SET_TAB_NOTIFICATIONS. Feature-detect, request only from a gesture, and degrade silently if unavailable. Never depend on notifications for critical payment state.

Also asked as: notifications permission q-app · hub notifications

chunks.title: How do I open Q-Mail or other apps for a user?
chunks.text:
## Q: How do I open Q-Mail or other apps for a user?

A: Navigate with qortal:// or LINK_TO_QDN_RESOURCE / OPEN_NEW_TAB to the target APP name used by that product. Do not scrape their private coordinates; use documented public identifiers and services. Fail soft if the app is unpublished on that node.

Also asked as: open q-mail from app · cross app open

chunks.title: What is GET_GROUPS_WITH_MEMBER?
chunks.text:
## Q: What is GET_GROUPS_WITH_MEMBER?

A: GET_GROUPS_WITH_MEMBER lists groups that include a member address (read-oriented; confirm approval needs for your version). Use it to personalize group UIs after Connect. Pair with LIST_GROUPS for broader discovery.

Also asked as: GET_GROUPS_WITH_MEMBER

chunks.title: What is TRANSFER_ASSET used for?
chunks.text:
## Q: What is TRANSFER_ASSET used for?

A: TRANSFER_ASSET moves assets with user approval (confirm params on target Hub). Explain asset name/amount in UI first. Like SEND_COIN, treat confirmation and any later notify/publish as separate steps.

Also asked as: TRANSFER_ASSET · asset transfer q-app

chunks.title: How do I integrate Hub back buttons with my SPA?
chunks.text:
## Q: How do I integrate Hub back buttons with my SPA?

A: Listen to popstate for in-app routes and integrate NAVIGATION_HISTORY when available. Ensure each pushState has a matching UI state. Do not break Hub-level back by replacing history incorrectly.

Also asked as: hub back button spa · popstate integration

chunks.title: What should be in a Q-App README for other developers?
chunks.text:
## Q: What should be in a Q-App README for other developers?

A: Document identifier prefixes, JSON schema versions, services used, publish rights (name ownership), Hub version tested, and example qortal:// links. Point to qortal.dev for actions. Clear conventions beat clever undocumented namespaces.

Also asked as: q-app readme conventions · document identifiers

chunks.title: What is SEARCH_CHAT_MESSAGES?
chunks.text:
## Q: What is SEARCH_CHAT_MESSAGES?

A: SEARCH_CHAT_MESSAGES searches chat on supported Hubs and may be approval-gated depending on version. Confirm parameters in qortal.dev. Do not treat chat search as a transactional ledger.

Also asked as: SEARCH_CHAT_MESSAGES

chunks.title: What is Qortal?
chunks.text:
## Q: What is Qortal?

A: Qortal is a fully decentralized blockchain and peer-to-peer data network — infrastructure for a parallel internet. People run their own nodes, mint QORT by contributing (minting), and use QDN to publish websites, Q-Apps, chat, and media without corporate cloud ownership. No ICO and no company owns the network. For orientation on QDN, open the Welcome to Qortal Q-App.

Also asked as: explain Qortal · what does Qortal do · tell me about Qortal · whats Qortal · what's Qortal · what is the Qortal network · how does Qortal work · define Qortal · describe Qortal · Qortal explained · is qortal decentralized · explain qortal simply · why should I use qortal

chunks.title: Is Qortal a video game?
chunks.text:
## Q: Is Qortal a video game?

A: No. Qortal is a fully decentralized blockchain and peer-to-peer data network. People run nodes, mint QORT by contributing, and publish on QDN. Levels are on-chain minting contribution levels.

Also asked as: is Qortal a game · Qortal online game · is Qortal like a Discord game

chunks.title: What is the native coin of Qortal?
chunks.text:
## Q: What is the native coin of Qortal?

A: The native coin is QORT. It pays transaction and QDN publish fees, is earned by minting (securing the network), and can be traded peer-to-peer on the Trade Portal for coins like LTC, BTC, DOGE, RVN, DGB, and ARRR. New QORT is created only by minting — there was no ICO and no pre-mine of cheap coins for early investors.

Also asked as: what is QORT · Qortal coin name · native currency

chunks.title: When was Qortal Genesis?
chunks.text:
## Q: When was Qortal Genesis?

A: Qortal mainnet Genesis — the first block — was minted on June 29, 2020. That is the network's birthday. Qortal was written from scratch after earlier work on QORA; Genesis started with nothing pre-mined for a privileged sale.

Also asked as: Qortal birthday · when did Qortal launch · Genesis date

chunks.title: What is minting on Qortal?
chunks.text:
## Q: What is minting on Qortal?

A: On Qortal, minting replaces mining. An account with an active minting key that stays online helps forge blocks and earns QORT. Reward share grows with your level (time spent minting). You cannot buy faster minting with expensive hardware — ordinary hardware (even a Raspberry Pi class machine) is enough. One minting account per person is the rule.

Also asked as: how does minting work · what is Proof of Contribution · earn QORT by minting · what is minting · what is mint · explain minting · minting on qortal

chunks.title: How do I become a minter?
chunks.text:
## Q: How do I become a minter?

A: ## How to become a minter

1. **Register a Qortal name** and keep a little QORT for fees.
2. **Run a synced full node** (Qortal Hub / Go / Core) and stay online.
3. Build a **visible track record** in the community (chat, helpful publishes).
4. Get a **Level 5+ minter** to nominate you in **Q-Mintership** (you cannot nominate yourself).
5. **Minter Admins** vote on-chain (~40% yes unlocks actions; ~40% admin signatures activate the MINTER group invite).
6. Accept **JOIN_GROUP**, add a minting account in **Q-Node**, and stay online.

Open **Q-Mintership** for the live nomination board, **Q-Minter Guide** for the full written walkthrough, and **Welcome to Qortal** for first steps. Sponsorship keys are obsolete.

Also asked as: how to start minting · get minting rights · become a Qortal minter · how to become a minter · how do i get minting rights · how to mint · how do i mint · how can i mint · how to mint on qortal · how do i mint qort · how do I get a minting nomination · how to get a nomination · how do I get nominated · get a minting nomination · how do I get nominated for minting · get nominated for minting · how to get nominated for minting

chunks.title: What are Qortal levels?
chunks.text:
## Q: What are Qortal levels?

A: Levels are on-chain account levels from minting contribution, ranging from 0 to 10 — not game scores. Level 0 is the waiting room (no reward share). Level 1 is Initiation (~7,200 blocks online). Level 5 is when you may nominate others (well over a year of sync). Level 10 is Maturity (~eight years of continuous contribution). Higher levels earn a larger share of each block reward and more voting weight.

Also asked as: explain levels · what do levels mean · level 1 to 10 · what is level on qortal · what is my level · how do levels work · how long to reach level 5 · qortal account levels

chunks.title: What is sponsorship or nomination?
chunks.text:
## Q: What is sponsorship or nomination?

A: On Qortal, a nomination is how someone becomes a minter (earning QORT with a full node). Sponsorship was the old path; nominations replaced it. A Level 5+ minter publishes a nomination card for you on the Q-Mintership Minter Board. Minter Admins vote; around 40% admin yes unlocks actions, then ~40% admin group-approval signatures activate your MINTER invite. You accept with JOIN_GROUP, add a minting account in Q-Node, and keep a synced full node online. You cannot nominate yourself. Open Q-Mintership for live cards and Q-Minter Guide for the written walkthrough.

Also asked as: what is sponsorship · nomination card · how does nomination work · what are nominations · explain nominations · minting nomination

chunks.title: Why is my seedphrase so important?
chunks.text:
## Q: Why is my seedphrase so important?

A: Your Qortal account is a keypair derived from the seedphrase; addresses start with "Q". The node holds no custody — there is no recovery service, support desk, or reset button. Losing the seedphrase means losing the account, names, and funds forever. Write it offline on paper (or another offline backup), never screenshot it into cloud photos, and never share it.

Also asked as: backup seed phrase · lost seedphrase · account recovery · is my seed phrase public · is seedphrase public · never share seed phrase · is my seedphrase public

chunks.title: Can someone recover my account if I lose my seedphrase?
chunks.text:
## Q: Can someone recover my account if I lose my seedphrase?

A: No. Nobody — not founders, admins, Hub, Core, or any support channel — can recover a lost seedphrase. Accounts are keys, not server records. If the seed is gone, the account is gone. Back it up offline before you fund the account or register a valuable name.

Also asked as: can support recover my wallet · forgot seedphrase · reset password Qortal · how do I recover my wallet · recover qortal wallet · restore wallet from seed · how to recover my account

chunks.title: What is a Qortal name?
chunks.text:
## Q: What is a Qortal name?

A: A registered on-chain name is your public identity and the anchor for everything you publish on QDN (websites, apps, files, avatars). Names are unique, tradeable, owned by your account, with no yearly registrar renewal. You must own a registered name before you can publish QDN resources. Registering costs a small QORT fee.

Also asked as: register a name · what are names for · Qortal username · what are qortal names · what are names on qortal · tell me about qortal names

chunks.title: What is QDN?
chunks.text:
## Q: What is QDN?

A: QDN (Qortal Data Network) is Qortal's decentralized data layer. Every resource is identified by a registered name, a service type (e.g. WEBSITE, APP, DOCUMENT, FILE), and an optional identifier. Nodes that follow a name store and serve that name's data. Large payloads are stored off-chain and verified by an on-chain SHA-256 hash; tiny payloads under 240 bytes can live fully on-chain.

Also asked as: what is the Qortal Data Network · explain QDN · how does QDN work

chunks.title: What is Q-Chat?
chunks.text:
## Q: What is Q-Chat?

A: Q-Chat is Qortal's built-in messenger: public groups, private groups, and direct messages. Chat messages are unconfirmed transactions — they carry no QORT fee and quietly expire after about 24 hours, so they are not permanent chain history. Accounts typically need a small QORT balance (around 4 QORT held, not spent) as an anti-spam gate before posting freely.

Also asked as: how does Q-Chat work · Qortal messaging · is Q-Chat free · what is private messaging on qortal · how do groups work · qortal groups chat · qortal dm

chunks.title: What are Q-Apps?
chunks.text:
## Q: What are Q-Apps?

A: Q-Apps are static web apps (HTML/JS/CSS) published on QDN, usually as a zip with index.html at the root, service type APP (max about 50 MB). They run inside Qortal Hub or Qortal GO with the qortalRequest bridge for wallet, publish, and payments — no private corporate backend required. Identity is your wallet address plus optional registered name.

Also asked as: what is a Q-App · Qortal applications · apps on Qortal

chunks.title: What is the Trade Portal?
chunks.text:
## Q: What is the Trade Portal?

A: The Trade Portal is built-in cross-chain trading. QORT trades directly for coins such as LTC, BTC, DOGE, RVN, DGB, and ARRR using AT (Automated Transaction) smart contracts — no centralized exchange or custodian. Prices come from open offers between users, not an order-matching company holding your coins.

Also asked as: how do I trade QORT · cross-chain trading · Q-Trade · what is trade portal · trade portal qortal · explain trade portal

chunks.title: Do I need to run a node?
chunks.text:
## Q: Do I need to run a node?

A: You can use Hub or Qortal GO against a node, but running your own node is full participation: you validate the chain, host QDN data for names you follow, can mint, and stay independent of gateways. In degraded-internet scenarios, locally synced chain and QDN content remain usable. A Raspberry Pi 4/5 with 4+ GB RAM and an SSD is a popular dedicated box; budget tens of GB of storage and room to grow.

Also asked as: should I run a node · why run Qortal Core · self-host Qortal · do I need my own node · must I run a node

chunks.title: How do fees work on Qortal?
chunks.text:
## Q: How do fees work on Qortal?

A: Transactions and QDN publishes cost small QORT fees, often proportional to data size. Fees are not taken by a company — they are shared among minters securing the network and help deter spam. Q-Chat messages typically cost no fee because they are unconfirmed and temporary. You need a little QORT on hand before you can register a name or publish.

Also asked as: transaction fees · how much does publishing cost · QORT fees

chunks.title: What is Qortal GO?
chunks.text:
## Q: What is Qortal GO?

A: Qortal GO is the native mobile (Android) client for Qortal — a pocket version of Hub capabilities: account access, QDN apps/websites, chat, trading flows, and more while you are away from a desktop node. It is still Qortal the network, not a separate game or social app. Keep your seedphrase backed up offline the same way as on desktop.

Also asked as: what is Qortal mobile · Qortal GO app · mobile Qortal · can I use qortal without a computer · qortal on phone only · use qortal on mobile only

chunks.title: What is Qortal Hub?
chunks.text:
## Q: What is Qortal Hub?

A: Qortal Hub is the modern desktop UI for your account, Q-Apps, QDN browsing, node interaction, minting tools, Trade Portal, and chat. It talks to Qortal Core (your node or a connected one). Hub embeds Q-Apps and injects qortalRequest so apps can use your wallet with your approval — your node, your rules.

Also asked as: what is the Hub · Qortal desktop app · Hub vs Core

chunks.title: Is there an ICO or pre-mine?
chunks.text:
## Q: Is there an ICO or pre-mine?

A: No. Qortal had no ICO and no pre-mine of cheap coins for early investors. Everyone begins at Level 0. The only way new QORT comes into being is by minting — showing up and helping hold the network. Influence cannot be bought with a big wallet; it is earned with time minting. QORT trades peer-to-peer on the built-in Trade Portal (not as a typical Binance listing story). The software clients are free to install; on-chain actions still need small QORT fees.

Also asked as: was there a token sale · premine · fair launch · is qortal a crypto scam · is qortal a scam · is qortal free · can I buy qort on binance · is qortal on binance

chunks.title: Can I buy minting power with better hardware?
chunks.text:
## Q: Can I buy minting power with better hardware?

A: No. Unlike proof-of-work mining races, Qortal minting does not reward faster or more expensive machines. You cannot buy your way to minting more QORT with ASIC farms. A modest always-on computer is enough; rewards are about contribution time and level, shared within tiers among online minters.

Also asked as: ASIC minting · GPU farming QORT · hardware advantage

chunks.title: What is Proof of Contribution?
chunks.text:
## Q: What is Proof of Contribution?

A: Proof of Contribution (minting) means you earn by keeping a minting account online and synchronized, helping secure the chain over time. It is light enough for ordinary hardware. Combined with nomination (Organic Proof of Humanity) and one minting account per person, it resists corporate farm capture that proof-of-work or pay-to-stake systems invite.

Also asked as: PoC explained · proof of contribution vs proof of work · how Qortal differs from Bitcoin mining

chunks.title: What are groups on Qortal?
chunks.text:
## Q: What are groups on Qortal?

A: On-chain groups provide shared membership, group chat, and group-managed permissions. Groups can be open or closed (invite/approval). Group-encrypted QDN data is readable only by members. Important network roles also use groups — for example the MINTER group invite after nomination approval.

Also asked as: explain groups · group chat Qortal · closed groups · how do I join a group on qortal · join a qortal group · how to join qortal group

chunks.title: How do I follow a name and why?
chunks.text:
## Q: How do I follow a name and why?

A: Following a name tells your node to host and serve that name's QDN data. Persistence is social: content stays alive because people who value it follow its publisher. For your own resilience, run a node that follows your own name so your publishes stay local. Popular content naturally gains redundancy across many nodes.

Also asked as: follow names · host someone's data · why follow on QDN

chunks.title: How do I publish data on QDN?
chunks.text:
## Q: How do I publish data on QDN?

A: 1. Own a registered name (publishing without one fails). 2. Choose a service type (WEBSITE, APP, DOCUMENT, FILE, IMAGE, etc.). 3. Optionally set an identifier (case-sensitive — keep a consistent scheme). 4. Publish; you pay a QORT fee proportional to size. Publishing again with the same name + service + identifier overwrites; only the current name owner can update.

Also asked as: publish to QDN · upload website Qortal · how to publish · how do I publish a website · how to publish a website on qortal · publish website qdn · how do I make a q-app · how to build a q-app

chunks.title: What happens if I sell my name?
chunks.text:
## Q: What happens if I sell my name?

A: Update rights move with the name. Only the current owner of the name can publish or overwrite resources under that name + service + identifier. If you sell or transfer the name, the buyer controls future updates to those QDN coordinates — plan publishes and transfers carefully.

Also asked as: transfer name ownership · sold my Qortal name · name sale rights

chunks.title: Addresses start with what letter?
chunks.text:
## Q: Addresses start with what letter?

A: Qortal account addresses start with the letter "Q". The account itself is a keypair derived from your seedphrase. The address is how payments and on-chain actions identify you; a registered name is the human-readable identity layered on top for QDN and public presence.

Also asked as: Qortal address format · what does a Qortal address look like

chunks.title: Who controls Qortal?
chunks.text:
## Q: Who controls Qortal?

A: No company owns Qortal. The community running nodes is the infrastructure. Even founders cannot shut it down — it keeps running while peers secure it. Governance uses on-chain votes with weight from minting level/time. Dev Admins steward core software updates by shared approval; Minter Admins handle minting nominations — elected roles, not thrones.

Also asked as: who owns Qortal · is Qortal a company · central authority

chunks.title: What is Organic Proof of Humanity?
chunks.text:
## Q: What is Organic Proof of Humanity?

A: It is the human nomination layer: a Level 5+ minter must vouch for you, Minter Admins approve, and the hard rule is one minting account per person. That stops corporations from spinning up hundreds of minting bots. You may hold multiple non-minting accounts, but only one minting account per human.

Also asked as: one account per person · anti Sybil minting · human verification Qortal

chunks.title: How often is a new block minted?
chunks.text:
## Q: How often is a new block minted?

A: A new block is minted about once every 60 seconds. Each block carries freshly minted QORT plus that block's transaction fees, shared among online minters by level tiers. Rewards are often tallied in batches (roughly every 1,000 blocks), so your balance may jump in steps rather than every minute.

Also asked as: block time · how fast are blocks · block reward timing

chunks.title: Do founders still get special rewards?
chunks.text:
## Q: Do founders still get special rewards?

A: Public team listings on qortal.dev/team name Jason Crowe as an original Qortal founder and Q-App developer (often known as Crowetic) and Ice as a founder and core developer, alongside other Dev Admins. Qortal itself is community-run infrastructure — no company owns the network. For a specific person's Level and publishes, use QDN mode name lookup.

chunks.title: Who is Crowetic?
chunks.text:
## Q: Who is Crowetic?

A: Crowetic is Jason Crowe — an original founder of Qortal and a long-time Q-App / ecosystem developer. Public team listings on qortal.dev/team name him among the founding contributors (alongside Ice and other Dev Admins). He also works on **NuQloud**, a project aimed at sovereign / decentralized cloud-style infrastructure aligned with Qortal’s self-hosted ethos. More about his work: [crowetic.com](https://crowetic.com). Qortal itself is community-run infrastructure with no company owner.

chunks.title: Is Qortal the same as Playing Qortal the book?
chunks.text:
## Q: Is Qortal the same as Playing Qortal the book?

A: No. Qortal is the decentralized blockchain and QDN network. Playing Qortal (by Simon James) is a philosophy book about the Revolution of Values — voluntary cooperation and sovereignty. Keep the network definition separate from the book.

Also asked as: Playing Qortal vs Qortal · is the book the network · Revolution of Values book

chunks.title: What hardware do I need for a node?
chunks.text:
## Q: What hardware do I need for a node?

A: Qortal Core is Java-based and runs on Linux, Windows, and macOS. A Raspberry Pi 4/5 class machine with 4+ GB RAM and an SSD is a popular dedicated node. Storage grows with the chain plus QDN content you follow — budget tens of GB and room to grow. A UPS pairs well with minting because rewards favor consistent uptime.

Also asked as: Raspberry Pi Qortal · node requirements · minimum specs

chunks.title: What if my node goes offline?
chunks.text:
## Q: What if my node goes offline?

A: Minting pauses while you are offline — you stop earning for that time. When you return, the node resyncs from peers; the chain itself is the backup. For QDN, others who follow the same names may still host the data, but following your own name on your node keeps your publishes resilient locally.

Also asked as: node offline minting · resync after downtime · missed blocks

chunks.title: How do I keep my account secure?
chunks.text:
## Q: How do I keep my account secure?

A: 1. Write the seedphrase offline and store it somewhere safe from fire, theft, and cloud sync. 2. Never share the seed or paste it into random apps. 3. Prefer your own node when you can. 4. Approve qortalRequest actions consciously — treat unexpected payment or publish prompts as suspicious. 5. Keep Core/Hub updated via the network's update mechanisms.

Also asked as: wallet security · protect my QORT · security best practices

chunks.title: Can I mint on multiple accounts?
chunks.text:
## Q: Can I mint on multiple accounts?

A: No for minting. The unbreakable rule is one minting account per person. You may keep multiple non-minting accounts and help many real humans join, but if several minting accounts are traced to one operator, they are all removed. That protects Organic Proof of Humanity.

Also asked as: multiple minting keys · two minter accounts · farm many accounts

chunks.title: What are Minter Admins?
chunks.text:
## Q: What are Minter Admins?

A: Minter Admins are community-elected members who review nomination cards and approve or remove minting rights by shared on-chain decision. Being an admin grants no extra vote weight in general governance; influence still comes from minting over time. To draw their admin reward share they must themselves be actively minting.

Also asked as: who are minter admins · minting approval · admin minting

chunks.title: What are Dev Admins?
chunks.text:
## Q: What are Dev Admins?

A: Dev Admins steward Qortal's core software. No network update ships until enough of them approve together. Because they contribute through development rather than uptime, they carry no minting requirement for that role. They are a separate group from Minter Admins.

Also asked as: who are dev admins · core software updates · who approves updates

chunks.title: How does voting work?
chunks.text:
## Q: How does voting work?

A: Qortal uses decentralized on-chain ballots. Higher minting level means more voting weight because you have contributed longer. Ideas can be brought to the community and put to a vote — influence is earned with time, not bought with a large QORT balance.

Also asked as: governance votes · voting weight · on-chain ballot

chunks.title: What is an AT trade?
chunks.text:
## Q: What is an AT trade?

A: AT means Automated Transaction — Qortal's smart-contract style mechanism used by the Trade Portal for cross-chain swaps. Your trade is peer-to-peer via the contract rules, not custody on a company exchange. Always understand the offer terms and keep enough balance for fees before you commit.

Also asked as: Automated Transaction · smart contract trade · how AT trading works

chunks.title: Do I need internet for Qortal forever?
chunks.text:
## Q: Do I need internet for Qortal forever?

A: Peers need some path to reach each other to sync and trade. Running your own node keeps your access independent of corporate gateways. In censored or degraded conditions, locally synced chain data and followed QDN content remain usable, and nodes can sync from any reachable peer — including community mesh paths where set up.

Also asked as: offline Qortal · censorship resistance access · degraded internet

chunks.title: What is Qortal Core?
chunks.text:
## Q: What is Qortal Core?

A: Qortal Core is the node software: it validates the blockchain, stores and serves QDN data for followed names, exposes a local API/UI, and participates in P2P peering. Hub and Qortal GO are user interfaces that talk to Core. Updates can ship through the network's auto-update mechanism — keep disk space healthy and Core current.

Also asked as: what is Core · node software · Qortal server process

chunks.title: Why do I need QORT before I can mint?
chunks.text:
## Q: Why do I need QORT before I can mint?

A: Almost every lasting on-chain action — registering a name, publishing, many transactions — needs a small QORT fee. You cannot mint until you are set up with minting rights, so newcomers need a little starter QORT first (community onboarding or a peer gift is common). Holding a small balance also unlocks free Q-Chat posting as an anti-spam gate.

Also asked as: starter QORT · need coins to begin · bootstrap fees · how much qort do I need to start · how much qort to begin · starter coins

chunks.title: What is the difference between WEBSITE and APP on QDN?
chunks.text:
## Q: What is the difference between WEBSITE and APP on QDN?

A: Both are multi-file QDN publishes. WEBSITE is for visitor-facing sites where missing paths 404. APP is for interactive apps and SPAs — missing paths fall through to index.html. APP max size is about 50 MB. Rule of thumb: client-side router and app behaviour → APP; mostly static pages with real 404s → WEBSITE.

Also asked as: WEBSITE vs APP · which service type for my site · SPA on QDN

chunks.title: How do I fetch a QDN resource?
chunks.text:
## Q: How do I fetch a QDN resource?

A: Specify the publisher's registered name, the service type, and the identifier (or omit identifier / use "default" for the default resource). Q-Apps use FETCH_QDN_RESOURCE via qortalRequest; public reads can also use the node's REST/fetch paths. If the data is not local yet, the node downloads it from peers following that name.

Also asked as: download from QDN · FETCH_QDN_RESOURCE · get a resource

chunks.title: What is a default QDN resource?
chunks.text:
## Q: What is a default QDN resource?

A: A resource published without an identifier is the default for that name + service — for example a user's main website is the default WEBSITE for their name. Apps can address it by omitting the identifier or using the keyword "default". Shared identifiers (like qortal_avatar) are the opposite idea: the same identifier across many names.

Also asked as: default identifier · main website resource · what does default mean on QDN

chunks.title: How do avatars work?
chunks.text:
## Q: How do avatars work?

A: Avatars use a shared identifier convention: service THUMBNAIL with identifier "qortal_avatar" under a user's registered name. Any app can fetch any user's avatar knowing only their name. THUMBNAIL is limited to about 500 KB, so keep avatar images small.

Also asked as: qortal_avatar · profile picture QDN · user thumbnail

chunks.title: Are private QDN resources possible?
chunks.text:
## Q: Are private QDN resources possible?

A: Yes. Private service variants (e.g. MAIL_PRIVATE, IMAGE_PRIVATE, DOCUMENT_PRIVATE) store data encrypted so only the intended recipient's private key can decrypt. Group-encrypted data is readable by group members. Public services are visible to anyone whose node can fetch them.

Also asked as: encrypted QDN · private mail · DOCUMENT_PRIVATE

chunks.title: What size limits should I know for QDN?
chunks.text:
## Q: What size limits should I know for QDN?

A: Common documented limits include: JSON about 25 KB; THUMBNAIL about 500 KB; IMAGE about 10 MB; APP about 50 MB; MAIL about 1 MB; CHAIN_COMMENT 239 bytes fully on-chain. Resources under 240 bytes can live fully on-chain; larger payloads are off-chain with an on-chain hash. Large files suit FILE service rather than stuffing DOCUMENT awkwardly.

Also asked as: QDN size limits · max APP size · how big can I publish

chunks.title: What coins can I trade for QORT?
chunks.text:
## Q: What coins can I trade for QORT?

A: Through the Trade Portal / AT trades you can trade QORT directly for coins such as LTC, BTC, DOGE, RVN, DGB, and ARRR (Pirate Chain), peer-to-peer without a custodial exchange. A Litecoin wallet is commonly created with your account to help bootstrap trading paths. Always verify offer details before committing.

Also asked as: trade BTC for QORT · supported trade pairs · LTC to QORT

chunks.title: Does Qortal use huge amounts of electricity?
chunks.text:
## Q: Does Qortal use huge amounts of electricity?

A: No. Minting is a light process suitable for a small always-on computer or Raspberry Pi sipping modest power — not a proof-of-work arms race of warehouses full of ASICs. A planet of Qortal minters would use a tiny fraction of what a single large proof-of-work coin burns.

Also asked as: energy use · is minting green · power consumption

chunks.title: What is QORA and how does it relate?
chunks.text:
## Q: What is QORA and how does it relate?

A: QORA was an earlier 2014-era blockchain. Builders later wrote Qortal from scratch with Genesis in 2020. Holders who burned QORA before Genesis were recorded as owed a slow repayment in QORT (historically 250 QORA per 1 QORT), funded by a small per-block share (settled at 1% after a 2022 community vote). It is a debt of honour, not a sale.

Also asked as: what is QORA · QORA burn · old coin repayment

chunks.title: How long to reach Level 5?
chunks.text:
## Q: How long to reach Level 5?

A: Reaching Level 5 takes well over a year of staying synchronized while minting — long enough to understand the network before you may nominate others. Exact timing depends on continuous online contribution; downtime slows progress. Level 5 is sometimes called Baptism in community language.

Also asked as: time to level 5 · when can I nominate · Baptism level

chunks.title: How long to reach Level 10?
chunks.text:
## Q: How long to reach Level 10?

A: Level 1 is about 7,200 online minted blocks. Credits are batched roughly every 1,000 blocks, so Level 1 often appears after about 8,000–9,000 online blocks. Trust the Level shown in Hub. Level 5+ can nominate new minters.

Also asked as: time to level 10 · Maturity level · max level

chunks.title: Why is my QORT balance jumping in steps?
chunks.text:
## Q: Why is my QORT balance jumping in steps?

A: Minting rewards are often tallied in batches, roughly every 1,000 blocks, rather than credited on every single ~60-second block. That is normal — do not assume minting is broken just because the balance is quiet between batch payouts. Also confirm your minting key is active and blocks-minted is increasing.

Also asked as: rewards not every block · batch payouts · balance not updating every minute

chunks.title: What is a minting key?
chunks.text:
## Q: What is a minting key?

A: A minting key is what lets an approved minting account forge blocks when online. In Hub, tools like the Q-Node app help create/add your minting account after you join the MINTER group. Keep the account's seedphrase backed up; the minting key is part of your participation setup, not a second recovery path for a lost seed.

Also asked as: add minting account · activate minting key · Q-Node minting

chunks.title: Can money buy voting power?
chunks.text:
## Q: Can money buy voting power?

A: No. Buying a large pile of QORT on the market does not buy extra votes, faster minting, or control. Voting weight comes from minting level/time. A wealthy newcomer still needs nomination, one minting account, and years of contribution — money is designed not to capture governance.

Also asked as: buy influence · whale voting · governance attack with money

chunks.title: What should I do on day one?
chunks.text:
## Q: What should I do on day one?

A: 1. Install Hub or Qortal GO and create an account. 2. Write your seedphrase offline immediately. 3. Obtain a little starter QORT and register a name. 4. Open Q-Chat and introduce yourself. 5. Optionally start a node or connect reliably so you can learn, publish something lasting, and eventually earn a nomination.

Also asked as: getting started · first steps on Qortal · onboarding checklist · how do I join qortal · how to join qortal · how do I get started on qortal · getting started on qortal · what do I need to use qortal · what do I need for qortal · requirements to use qortal

chunks.title: Is Qortal censorship resistant?
chunks.text:
## Q: Is Qortal censorship resistant?

A: Qortal is built so identity, data, and apps live on peer-run infrastructure rather than a company server that can flip a switch. Anyone can run a node, follow names, and host data. Persistence still depends on peers following and serving content — so follow what matters, run your own node when you can, and publish under your own name.

Also asked as: censorship · can Qortal be shut down · decentralized publishing

chunks.title: What is qortalRequest?
chunks.text:
## Q: What is qortalRequest?

A: qortalRequest is the JavaScript bridge Hub and Qortal GO inject into embedded Q-Apps. Apps call it for wallet identity, payments, publishing, encryption, and navigation — always with user approval for sensitive actions. Use try/catch; call identity actions from a user gesture (button), not automatically on first paint.

Also asked as: qortalRequest bridge · how Q-Apps talk to wallet · Hub API for apps

chunks.title: Do Q-Chat messages stay forever?
chunks.text:
## Q: Do Q-Chat messages stay forever?

A: No. Q-Chat messages are unconfirmed transactions that typically vanish after about 24 hours and are not permanent blockchain history. That is why they carry no fee. For lasting communication or records, use on-chain transactions, Q-Mail/private resources, or published QDN documents — depending on your need.

Also asked as: Q-Chat history · are chats permanent · messages disappear

chunks.title: What ports does a node use?
chunks.text:
## Q: What ports does a node use?

A: Qortal peers over its own P2P port and serves a local API/UI for Hub and Q-Apps. Port forwarding improves peer connectivity but is not strictly required to use the network. The trust model is intentional: apps talk to your local node API, not a mandatory third-party cloud API.

Also asked as: port forwarding · P2P port · local API

chunks.title: How do I verify minting is working?
chunks.text:
## Q: How do I verify minting is working?

A: On your node/Hub minting views, confirm the minting key is active and that blocks-minted (or equivalent progress) is increasing over time while you stay synced. Remember rewards may credit in batches (~1,000 blocks). Also watch disk space and that Core stays updated.

Also asked as: check if minting · minting not earning · blocks minted

chunks.title: Will anyone ask for my seedphrase?
chunks.text:
## Q: Will anyone ask for my seedphrase?

A: Legitimate helpers never need your seedphrase. Anyone asking for it is attempting theft. Mentors can guide clicks and concepts; they cannot "type the seed for you" safely. Hang up on seed requests immediately.

Also asked as: seedphrase scam · support asked for seed

chunks.title: What remains usable if the wider internet degrades?
chunks.text:
## Q: What remains usable if the wider internet degrades?

A: Locally synced blockchain data, QDN content your node already follows/hosts, local Hub/GO against your node, and mesh paths like Reticulum where configured. Design your setup assuming gateways and corporate clouds may vanish.

Also asked as: grid down Qortal · local-only usefulness

chunks.title: How does the new nomination system work?
chunks.text:
## Q: How does the new nomination system work?

A: Nomination is Qortal’s process for granting minting rights (replacing old sponsorship). 1) A Level 5+ minter publishes your nomination card in Q-Mintership. 2) A poll opens (admin votes counted separately). 3) ~40% Minter Admin yes unlocks actions. 4) An admin creates a MINTER group invite; ~40% admin signatures activate it. 5) You JOIN_GROUP, add a minting account in Q-Node, and keep a synced full node online to earn QORT. You cannot nominate yourself. Open Q-Mintership for the live board and Q-Minter Guide for details.

chunks.title: What can I do on Qortal?
chunks.text:
## Q: What can I do on Qortal?

A: On Qortal you can: run a full node; mint QORT once you have minting rights (Proof of Contribution); register a name; publish websites and Q-Apps on QDN; chat in groups/DMs; share media (Q-Tube and friends); trade/trade assets where apps support it; follow names; and explore community Q-Apps (Welcome to Qortal is a good first stop). Minting is optional — non-minters can still hold QORT, publish, chat, and use apps. This is about the network itself, not any book.

chunks.title: What is a Qortal node?
chunks.text:
## Q: What is a Qortal node?

A: A Qortal node (Qortal Core) is software that validates the blockchain, talks to peers, and can host QDN data. Hub and Qortal GO are the UIs that talk to a node — your own or a connected one. Syncing means downloading and verifying blocks until you are caught up with the network; keep the node online and give it disk space. Running your own node is optional for browsing but required for full independence and minting.

Also asked as: what is a node · what is qortal core · how do I sync my node · sync my node · node syncing · explain qortal node

chunks.title: Can I mint without a nomination?
chunks.text:
## Q: Can I mint without a nomination?

A: No. Minting rights come through nomination: a Level 5+ minter publishes your card in Q-Mintership, Minter Admins vote, you accept the MINTER group invite, then add a minting account in Q-Node and stay online. You cannot enable minting alone. Until then you can still hold QORT, chat, register a name, and publish on QDN.

Also asked as: mint without nomination · do I need nomination to mint · minting without being nominated

chunks.title: How do I send QORT to someone?
chunks.text:
## Q: How do I send QORT to someone?

A: In Hub or Qortal GO, open the payment / send flow, enter the recipient’s Qortal address (starts with Q) or a registered name if the UI resolves it, set the amount, confirm the fee, and approve the transaction. Double-check the address — on-chain sends are irreversible. Keep a little extra QORT for fees. Nobody legitimate will ask you to “test send” by sharing your seedphrase.

Also asked as: send qort · how to send qort · transfer qort · pay someone in qort · how do I send qort to someone

chunks.title: Can I use Qortal without a computer?
chunks.text:
## Q: Can I use Qortal without a computer?

A: Yes for everyday use: Qortal GO on Android lets you hold an account, chat, browse QDN, and trade flows from a phone. A full always-on node and minting still usually want a dedicated computer (or mini-PC / Raspberry Pi) left online. Many people use GO on the go and keep Core on a home machine.

Also asked as: qortal without pc · do I need a computer for qortal · phone only qortal

chunks.title: What is the price of QORT?
chunks.text:
## Q: What is the price of QORT?

A: There is no single official QORT price — peer offers set the rate. LTC is the main QORT market. Switch to the QDN chat window and ask again: QDN mode can read a live QORT/LTC peer estimate from your connected node’s Trade Portal data. Offline will not invent USD/BTC figures. You can also open the Trade Portal or discuss rates in QDN Chat.

Also asked as: how much is QORT · QORT price · QORT to USD · QORT value · what is QORT worth · how much does QORT cost · QORT exchange rate · current QORT price · price of qort coin · QORT to LTC · QORT LTC price · how much QORT in LTC · LTC per QORT · price of QORT in LTC

chunks.title: What is Q-Mail?
chunks.text:
## Q: What is Q-Mail?

A: Q-Mail is Qortal's mail-style messaging on the network, including private encrypted variants. Unlike fleeting Q-Chat, mail-oriented resources are meant as lasting messages with size limits (MAIL around 1 MB). Use it when you need a message that should persist beyond a day's chat buffer.

Also asked as: Qortal mail · send Q-Mail · private messages lasting

chunks.title: What is Q-Tube?
chunks.text:
## Q: What is Q-Tube?

A: Q-Tube is a community Q-App ecosystem for publishing and watching videos on QDN — decentralized media under registered names, hosted by nodes that follow those names. Publish video resources under your name; viewers fetch from peers rather than a corporate video host.

Also asked as: Qortal video · publish videos · decentralized YouTube

chunks.title: What is Q-Share?
chunks.text:
## Q: What is Q-Share?

A: Q-Share is for sharing files on QDN under your registered name. Publish with an appropriate FILE/FILES service, pay the size-based fee, and people who follow your name (or fetch the resource) can retrieve it from the peer network.

Also asked as: share files on Qortal · QDN file sharing

chunks.title: What is Subwire?
chunks.text:
## Q: What is Subwire?

A: Subwire is a blogging-style Q-App ecosystem on Qortal where people publish blog content via QDN services (such as BLOG / BLOG_COMMENT patterns). Your posts live under your registered name on the peer network rather than a corporate blog host.

Also asked as: Qortal blog · blogging app · BLOG_POST

chunks.title: What is the Qortal Web Builder?
chunks.text:
## Q: What is the Qortal Web Builder?

A: QWB (Qortal Web Builder) is a no-code / drag-and-drop way to build a site and publish it to QDN under your name — useful on day one when you want a lasting presence without writing code. The result is still a normal QDN WEBSITE (or similar) resource peers can host.

Also asked as: QWB · build website without code · drag and drop site

chunks.title: What is a QORTector?
chunks.text:
## Q: What is a QORTector?

A: A QORTector is a plug-and-play node appliance idea — dedicated hardware so you can keep a node (and minting) running without tying up your main computer. Same network rules apply: back up your seedphrase offline and keep the device powered and synced.

Also asked as: plug and play node · dedicated node box

chunks.title: How do identifiers work on QDN?
chunks.text:
## Q: How do identifiers work on QDN?

A: The optional identifier string distinguishes multiple resources for the same name + service. Identifiers are case-sensitive — "MyApp_config" and "myapp_config" are different. Apps should prefix identifiers with their app name (e.g. myapp_ + suffix) and later search with that prefix. Always validate fetched data; QDN is permissionless.

Also asked as: QDN identifier · case sensitive identifier · app prefix identifiers

chunks.title: Can I update a published resource?
chunks.text:
## Q: Can I update a published resource?

A: Yes. Publish again with the same name + service + identifier and the new version overwrites for fetchers. Only the current owner of the name can update. There is no separate "edit password" — control of the name is control of updates.

Also asked as: overwrite QDN · edit published data · update website on Qortal

chunks.title: What is CHAIN_COMMENT?
chunks.text:
## Q: What is CHAIN_COMMENT?

A: CHAIN_COMMENT is a tiny fully on-chain payload service capped at 239 bytes. Use it for small permanent comments anchored in the chain itself. Larger discussion or content belongs in off-chain QDN services with on-chain hashes.

Also asked as: on-chain comment · 239 bytes · tiny on-chain data

chunks.title: What happens to data if nobody follows a name?
chunks.text:
## Q: What happens to data if nobody follows a name?

A: QDN persistence is follow-based. If no node follows a name, that name's hosted payloads can become hard to fetch. Popular content gains redundancy; obscure content needs friends, mirrors, or your own always-on node following your name. Social hosting is a feature, not a bug — value what you want to keep alive.

Also asked as: data disappearance · unfollowed content · QDN persistence

chunks.title: How do I register a name step by step?
chunks.text:
## Q: How do I register a name step by step?

A: 1. Create an account and securely back up the seedphrase. 2. Obtain enough QORT for the name fee (community onboarding often helps newcomers). 3. In Hub or GO, open the name registration flow and choose a unique name. 4. Confirm the transaction on-chain. 5. After confirmation, you can publish QDN resources under that name.

Also asked as: buy a name · claim username · name registration steps · how do I register a name on qortal · how to register a name · register name on qortal

chunks.title: Are names renewed every year?
chunks.text:
## Q: Are names renewed every year?

A: No corporate registrar renewal. Once your account owns the name on-chain, it remains yours until you transfer or sell it. Protect the seedphrase — losing the account loses the name with it.

Also asked as: name expiration · renew Qortal name · annual name fee

chunks.title: What is Level 0?
chunks.text:
## Q: What is Level 0?

A: Level 0 is where you begin after minting approval — the waiting room. Level 0 earns nothing from the block reward share. After roughly 7,200 blocks of staying online (~one week), you cross into Level 1 (Initiation) and begin earning as an online minter in your tier.

Also asked as: level zero · before level 1 · waiting room level

chunks.title: Can corporations farm QORT?
chunks.text:
## Q: Can corporations farm QORT?

A: The design pushes back hard: nomination is a human handshake, one minting account per person, and multi-account farms get removed. Paying workers to beg nominations for phantom accounts is brittle compared to those workers simply minting for themselves. Money alone cannot buy minting rights or vote weight.

Also asked as: corporate capture · bot farms · Sybil resistance

chunks.title: Is there a maximum QORT supply?
chunks.text:
## Q: Is there a maximum QORT supply?

A: Unlike Bitcoin's hard 21 million cap, Qortal has no maximum supply ceiling of that style. New QORT is minted continuously to online minters so there is always issuance for contribution. Emission rate steps down over years and can be community-adjusted within guardrails.

Also asked as: max supply · infinite supply · tokenomics cap

chunks.title: What is the 1% QORA repayment share?
chunks.text:
## Q: What is the 1% QORA repayment share?

A: A small per-block share (1% after a 2022 community vote; it was larger earlier) slowly repays people who burned QORA before Genesis, at a fixed rate of 250 old QORA per 1 QORT. Recipients need not mint — the network remembers the debt. It will take many years to pay in full.

Also asked as: QORA debt · 1 percent block share · burn repayment

chunks.title: Do I need port forwarding to mint?
chunks.text:
## Q: Do I need port forwarding to mint?

A: Port forwarding improves peer connectivity but is not strictly required to use the network or begin participating. Prioritize a stable machine, synced Core, active minting key, and offline seedphrase backup. Improve networking if you see poor peer counts.

Also asked as: NAT minting · router ports required

chunks.title: How much storage does a node need?
chunks.text:
## Q: How much storage does a node need?

A: Budget tens of GB to start for chain data plus whatever QDN content you follow and host, with room to grow as the chain and your follows expand. Prefer an SSD. Monitor free disk — a full disk stops a healthy node faster than almost anything else.

Also asked as: disk space · blockchain size · storage planning

chunks.title: Should I use a UPS with minting?
chunks.text:
## Q: Should I use a UPS with minting?

A: Yes if you can. Minting rewards consistent uptime; power blips mean downtime and slower level progress. An uninterruptible power supply for a Pi or small PC is a practical pairing with an always-on node.

Also asked as: battery backup node · power outage minting

chunks.title: How do Core updates work?
chunks.text:
## Q: How do Core updates work?

A: Keep Core updated; updates can ship through the network's auto-update mechanism after Dev Admin approval processes. Also keep an eye on disk space and that the node restarts cleanly after updates. Running ancient Core invites sync and compatibility pain.

Also asked as: auto update · upgrade Qortal Core · node version

chunks.title: What is the local trust model?
chunks.text:
## Q: What is the local trust model?

A: Hub and Q-Apps talk to your own node's local API/UI. That is intentional: your node, your rules, no mandatory third-party API dependency. Prefer verifying important actions on hardware you control, especially for minting and large publishes.

Also asked as: local API trust · why run own node for apps

chunks.title: Can I use Qortal without registering a name?
chunks.text:
## Q: Can I use Qortal without registering a name?

A: You can hold an account and receive QORT with just an address, but a registered name is required to publish QDN resources and is the practical public identity for apps, sites, and being known in the community. Most newcomers register a name early.

Also asked as: no name account · publish without name · address only

chunks.title: What are shared identifiers?
chunks.text:
## Q: What are shared identifiers?

A: Shared identifiers are deterministic locations used across many names — for example every avatar uses THUMBNAIL + "qortal_avatar". Apps agree on the identifier string so they can find the same kind of resource for any name without a central profile server.

Also asked as: cross-app identifiers · deterministic QDN paths

chunks.title: How should apps name their QDN identifiers?
chunks.text:
## Q: How should apps name their QDN identifiers?

A: Prefix with the app slug, e.g. myapp_config_v1 or myapp_post_<id>. Later search with SEARCH_QDN_RESOURCES using the prefix option. Because QDN is permissionless, validate the schema of everything you fetch — an identifier match is not proof your app wrote it.

Also asked as: identifier namespace · SEARCH_QDN_RESOURCES prefix · app data conventions

chunks.title: What is the APP 50 MB limit?
chunks.text:
## Q: What is the APP 50 MB limit?

A: Q-Apps published as service APP are multi-file zips with a typical maximum around 50 MB. Stay under the limit, ship assets inside the zip (avoid CDN dependencies), and use relative paths with a flat dist layout so Hub/GO can serve the app offline-friendly.

Also asked as: max Q-App size · APP zip too large

chunks.title: Why did my Q-App show a grey screen?
chunks.text:
## Q: Why did my Q-App show a grey screen?

A: Common causes: zip layout wrong (index.html not at root), bundler base path not "./" so assets 404, Hub opening /render/APP/Name without a trailing slash so relative assets resolve badly, or relying on external CDNs blocked offline. Rebuild, flatten dist, re-zip, and republish.

Also asked as: Q-App blank screen · assets 404 · SPA path bug

chunks.title: WEBSITE missing file returns what?
chunks.text:
## Q: WEBSITE missing file returns what?

A: On QDN WEBSITE service, a missing file path returns 404. On APP service, missing paths fall through to index.html for SPA routing. Choosing the wrong service type is a frequent publishing mistake.

Also asked as: WEBSITE 404 · APP fallback index

chunks.title: What is FILE vs DOCUMENT on QDN?
chunks.text:
## Q: What is FILE vs DOCUMENT on QDN?

A: Use FILE/FILES for large binary or general file payloads. DOCUMENT is for document-style payloads; do not force huge binaries into the wrong service. JSON is for small structured metadata (~25 KB). Pick the service that matches validation rules and size expectations.

Also asked as: FILE service · DOCUMENT service · which service for large files

chunks.title: Can resources live fully on-chain?
chunks.text:
## Q: Can resources live fully on-chain?

A: Yes if they are under about 240 bytes (CHAIN_COMMENT max 239 bytes is the clear example). Larger payloads are stored off-chain on QDN and verified by an on-chain SHA-256 hash. That keeps the chain lean while data remains integrity-checked.

Also asked as: on-chain vs off-chain data · SHA-256 verification · 240 bytes

chunks.title: How do private groups help?
chunks.text:
## Q: How do private groups help?

A: Closed groups use invite/approval membership. They enable private group chat and group-encrypted QDN data readable only by members — useful for teams, families, or communities who want shared private publishing without a company chat server.

Also asked as: invite only group · group encrypted data

chunks.title: Open vs closed groups?
chunks.text:
## Q: Open vs closed groups?

A: Open groups allow broader joining; closed groups require invite or approval. Both are on-chain membership structures with chat and permission features. Pick closed when membership itself is part of the security boundary.

Also asked as: public group · approval group

chunks.title: How do I send QORT to someone?
chunks.text:
## Q: How do I send QORT to someone?

A: Use Hub or Qortal GO's send/payment flow: enter the recipient's Qortal address (starts with Q) or use a supported payment QR / qortal://pay deep link, set the amount, confirm the fee, and approve the transaction. Double-check the address — on-chain sends are final.

Also asked as: pay QORT · transfer coins · payment QR

chunks.title: What are qortal:// links?
chunks.text:
## Q: What are qortal:// links?

A: qortal:// deep links open QDN resources, apps, or payment flows inside Hub or Qortal GO. On Android, Qortal GO can register app links for gateway hosts and qortal:// payment links so scans open the right screen. They are network-native links, not generic web URLs.

Also asked as: deep links · qortal protocol links · open in GO

chunks.title: Is Trade Portal custodial?
chunks.text:
## Q: Is Trade Portal custodial?

A: No. Trades use AT contracts peer-to-peer. There is no exchange company holding your coins as custodian. You still must understand offer terms, wait for confirmations as the flow requires, and protect your seedphrase — non-custodial does not mean risk-free.

Also asked as: custodial exchange · who holds trade funds · non-custodial trading

chunks.title: Can I trade without KYC on a company exchange?
chunks.text:
## Q: Can I trade without KYC on a company exchange?
