A: Trade Portal AT trades are peer-to-peer on Qortal infrastructure without a corporate exchange KYC desk. You still need the foreign coin wallet paths the trade requires (e.g. LTC) and enough QORT for fees. Follow local laws that apply to you; the tech itself is non-custodial P2P.

Also asked as: KYC free trade · P2P without exchange account

chunks.title: What foreign wallets are involved in trading?
chunks.text:
## Q: What foreign wallets are involved in trading?

A: Cross-chain trades need the other chain's coin. Accounts commonly get a Litecoin wallet automatically to help LTC↔QORT paths; other pairs involve their respective coins (BTC, DOGE, RVN, DGB, ARRR, etc.). Keep those keys/seed backups as carefully as your Qortal seed.

Also asked as: Litecoin wallet Qortal · BTC trade wallet

chunks.title: What is Reticulum in relation to Qortal?
chunks.text:
## Q: What is Reticulum in relation to Qortal?

A: Qortal also runs over Reticulum mesh networking paths in the ecosystem — useful when conventional internet is weak. Voice calls have been available on desktop and on mobile Android GO builds. Think user-owned mesh plus Qortal-native apps, not a cloud phone company.

Also asked as: Reticulum mesh · LoRa Qortal · mesh voice

chunks.title: Who is Simon James in Playing Qortal?
chunks.text:
## Q: Who is Simon James in Playing Qortal?

A: Simon James is the author of the book Playing Qortal, which teaches the Revolution of Values philosophy. That is separate from the technical definition of Qortal as a blockchain and QDN network.

Also asked as: Playing Qortal author · who wrote Playing Qortal

chunks.title: What is the Revolution of Values?
chunks.text:
## Q: What is the Revolution of Values?

A: It is the philosophical frame associated with Playing Qortal: shifting from extractive money-first culture toward voluntary cooperation, gratitude, and personal sovereignty — with Qortal as shared infrastructure people run themselves. Ask for philosophy when you want that layer; ask "what is Qortal" when you want the network definition.

Also asked as: Qortal philosophy · values revolution

chunks.title: What does MINTER group invite mean?
chunks.text:
## Q: What does MINTER group invite mean?

A: After Minter Admins approve your nomination, you receive an invitation to the MINTER group. Accept it, then add your minting account (e.g. via Q-Node). Group approval thresholds involve a fraction of admins signing — exact numbers shift as the admin set grows.

Also asked as: join MINTER group · minting invite · group approval signatures

chunks.title: Can minting rights be removed?
chunks.text:
## Q: Can minting rights be removed?

A: Yes. Minter Admins can remove minting rights by shared on-chain decision — especially for rules violations like multi-account minting farms. Minting is a community-granted responsibility, not an irreversible purchased privilege.

Also asked as: lose minting · minting revoked · removed from minters

chunks.title: Do admins get extra vote power?
chunks.text:
## Q: Do admins get extra vote power?

A: Admin roles are paid responsibilities for specific jobs (nominations or software stewardship), not general thrones. Genuine influence on Qortal still comes from minting over time. Minter Admins must actively mint to draw their admin reward share.

Also asked as: admin voting power · are admins above others

chunks.title: What percentage do admins currently receive?
chunks.text:
## Q: What percentage do admins currently receive?

A: Community documentation describes admins receiving a base share plus temporary redirection from empty high-level tiers and former founder share — on the order of about 35% combined for Minter and Dev Admins (~17.5% each) at that snapshot, split among individuals. When top tiers fill with real minters, that redirected portion returns to minters by design. Treat percentages as evolving with votes and tier occupancy.

Also asked as: admin reward share · 35 percent block

chunks.title: Why is Levels 9–10 empty important?
chunks.text:
## Q: Why is Levels 9–10 empty important?

A: Until minters reach the top tiers, that tier's designed reward slice may be temporarily redirected (e.g. toward admins) rather than sitting unused. Once real minters occupy Levels 9–10, that share flows to them as designed. Empty tiers are a young-network fact, not a permanent tax.

Also asked as: empty top tiers · level 9 reward redirect

chunks.title: How do I back up correctly?
chunks.text:
## Q: How do I back up correctly?

A: Write the full seedphrase on paper (or another offline medium), verify you can read every word, store copies in separate safe places, and never put the seed in email, cloud notes, or chat. Test recovery on a spare device only when you understand the risk. The backup is the account.

Also asked as: how to backup wallet · paper backup · seedphrase storage

chunks.title: Should I screenshot my seedphrase?
chunks.text:
## Q: Should I screenshot my seedphrase?

A: Avoid it. Phone screenshots often sync to cloud photo backups — exactly the failure mode that loses sovereignty. Prefer handwritten offline copies. If a screen display is unavoidable temporarily, do not leave it in gallery sync; move to offline storage and delete synced copies.

Also asked as: seed screenshot · cloud photos seed

chunks.title: Can Hub custodially hold my coins?
chunks.text:
## Q: Can Hub custodially hold my coins?

A: No. Hub and Core do not custody accounts as server logins. Your keys are yours. If you lose the seedphrase, no Hub button can restore the account. That is inconvenient by design — it is self-sovereignty.

Also asked as: is Hub custodial · password reset wallet

chunks.title: How do I restore an account on a new phone?
chunks.text:
## Q: How do I restore an account on a new phone?

A: Install Qortal GO (or Hub), choose restore/import, enter the seedphrase carefully offline, and verify the address matches what you expect before you move funds. Never type a seed into a random APK from an untrusted source. After restore, re-establish node connection settings you trust.

Also asked as: import seedphrase · restore on Android · move to new device

chunks.title: What is gateway mode?
chunks.text:
## Q: What is gateway mode?

A: Sometimes UIs connect through a public gateway when you are not running local Core. Convenient, but the sovereignty ideal is your own node. Sensitive workflows and true independence favor local Core; gateways are helpers, not the long-term trust model.

Also asked as: public gateway · not using local node

chunks.title: Why follow my own name on my node?
chunks.text:
## Q: Why follow my own name on my node?

A: So your published apps, sites, and documents are always held locally on hardware you control. Even if other followers drop away temporarily, your node still has your data. Encourage friends to follow names that matter to them for social redundancy.

Also asked as: self follow · host my own publishes

chunks.title: What is data hosting socially?
chunks.text:
## Q: What is data hosting socially?

A: QDN storage is follow-based: nodes host data for names they follow. Content survives because communities care enough to host it. That is different from paying a cloud bill to one company — persistence is earned by relevance and relationships.

Also asked as: social storage · follow-based hosting

chunks.title: Can I host data for friends?
chunks.text:
## Q: Can I host data for friends?

A: Yes — follow their registered names on your node. You help keep their QDN resources available to the network. This is one of the most practical ways to support creators you value without a platform middleman.

Also asked as: pin friend's name · help host QDN

chunks.title: What media services exist on QDN?
chunks.text:
## Q: What media services exist on QDN?

A: Common ones include IMAGE (~10 MB), THUMBNAIL (~500 KB), VIDEO, AUDIO, FILE/FILES, plus app/site packages WEBSITE and APP. Private variants encrypt for a recipient. Choose the service that matches the content type and size.

Also asked as: VIDEO service · AUDIO on QDN · media publishing

chunks.title: What is GAME service on QDN?
chunks.text:
## Q: What is GAME service on QDN?

A: GAME is a QDN service type for game-related resources some apps publish — one content category on the data network, like IMAGE or DOCUMENT. It does not change what the Qortal network itself is: a blockchain and peer-to-peer data network.

Also asked as: QDN GAME type · games on QDN

chunks.title: How do JSON resources differ?
chunks.text:
## Q: How do JSON resources differ?

A: JSON service is for small structured metadata with a tight limit (~25 KB). Ideal for manifests, configs, and indexes. Larger documents should use DOCUMENT or FILE. Apps often publish a JSON manifest then point to bigger assets.

Also asked as: JSON 25KB · manifest on QDN

chunks.title: How do I publish a JSON document from a Q-App?
chunks.text:
## Q: How do I publish a JSON document from a Q-App?

A: Own a name, then call qortalRequest with action PUBLISH_QDN_RESOURCE, setting name, service "DOCUMENT" or "JSON" as appropriate, a clear identifier, and data64 (UTF-8-safe base64 of your payload). Handle errors if the name is missing or the fee balance is too low.

Also asked as: PUBLISH_QDN_RESOURCE example · publish JSON

chunks.title: Why validate anything fetched from QDN?
chunks.text:
## Q: Why validate anything fetched from QDN?

A: QDN is permissionless — anyone can publish under their own name, and identifiers can be mimicked across names. An app must validate format and trust the publisher name it intends, not assume an identifier string alone means "safe" or "official."

Also asked as: untrusted QDN data · validate fetches

chunks.title: What is SEARCH_QDN_RESOURCES?
chunks.text:
## Q: What is SEARCH_QDN_RESOURCES?

A: It is the search action/API pattern Q-Apps use to find resources, often filtering by service and identifier prefix. Use app-prefixed identifiers so your search returns your app's data cluster, then validate each result.

Also asked as: search QDN · find resources by prefix

chunks.title: Can I publish a multi-file website from inside a Q-App?
chunks.text:
## Q: Can I publish a multi-file website from inside a Q-App?

A: Fetching multi-file WEBSITE/APP resources is supported, but publishing multi-file packages from inside a Q-App is limited or unavailable in many Hub builds — use the Hub UI publish flow for zips. Always verify against your running Hub/Core version.

Also asked as: publish zip from Q-App · multi-file publish limits

chunks.title: Should Q-Apps call GET_USER_ACCOUNT on page load?
chunks.text:
## Q: Should Q-Apps call GET_USER_ACCOUNT on page load?

A: No. Identity actions are gesture-gated — call them from a button click so the user consciously approves. Auto-prompting on first paint creates bad UX and looks like phishing. Detect the bridge, show UI, then request account on demand.

Also asked as: GET_USER_ACCOUNT · wallet permission UX

chunks.title: What offline rule should Q-Apps follow?
chunks.text:
## Q: What offline rule should Q-Apps follow?

A: Ship assets inside the zip; use relative paths; avoid CDN scripts that vanish offline. Qortal users and Qortino itself may be offline or mesh-only. An app that requires the corporate web is fighting the platform's purpose.

Also asked as: offline-first Q-App · no CDN

chunks.title: Can I mint from my phone alone?
chunks.text:
## Q: Can I mint from my phone alone?

A: Minting wants reliable uptime. Phones sleep, change networks, and are poor always-on minters. Practical setup: a dedicated node (Pi/PC/QORTector) stays online minting; phone GO is for daily use, chat, apps, and management. Keep the seed backed up either way.

Also asked as: mint on Android · phone minting uptime

chunks.title: What are the Golden Rules about?
chunks.text:
## Q: What are the Golden Rules about?

A: Community golden rules emphasize staying synchronized and minting when you can, and helping people you love join so they can mint their own sovereignty too. Teach installation of Core, Hub, or GO when someone is stuck. The spirit is mutual aid, not extractive farming.

Also asked as: Golden Rules of the Game · help others join

chunks.title: What is Initiation, Baptism, Maturity?
chunks.text:
## Q: What is Initiation, Baptism, Maturity?

A: Community names for milestones: Initiation ≈ Level 1; Baptism ≈ the long path to Level 5 (may nominate); Maturity ≈ Level 10. They describe contribution age in the community, not video-game achievements.

Also asked as: Baptism minting · maturity milestone

chunks.title: Why do early minters hold more QORT?
chunks.text:
## Q: Why do early minters hold more QORT?

A: Someone always goes first; earlier continuous minters simply spent more time earning. That is not a permanent throne — everyone can climb toward Level 10 equality of standing, and even early people stop earning if they go offline. The design pays time, not a privileged sale.

Also asked as: early adopter advantage · is Qortal unfair to newcomers

chunks.title: How does community writing contrast Qortal with Bitcoin?
chunks.text:
## Q: How does community writing contrast Qortal with Bitcoin?

A: The contrast drawn is that proof-of-work coins tend to concentrate in those who can afford industrial mining, while Qortal lets ordinary people mint on modest hardware with human nomination — ownership of issuance tied to participation time, not capital expenditure.

Also asked as: Bitcoin vs Qortal · people's Bitcoin

chunks.title: Do I pay monthly to host a website on Qortal?
chunks.text:
## Q: Do I pay monthly to host a website on Qortal?

A: There is no classic monthly web-host bill. You pay QORT fees when you publish/update, and persistence depends on nodes following your name (including your own). Popular sites gain many hosts; your own node is your best insurance.

Also asked as: free hosting · no monthly web bill · host forever

chunks.title: What is Qortal Web?
chunks.text:
## Q: What is Qortal Web?

A: Qortal Web refers to browsing the decentralized web of WEBSITE/APP resources on QDN through Hub/GO — sites published under names, served by peers. It is the user-facing web layer of QDN, not a separate corporate internet.

Also asked as: browse QDN websites · decentralized web

chunks.title: How do voice calls work in the ecosystem?
chunks.text:
## Q: How do voice calls work in the ecosystem?

A: Voice calls have been available on desktop and on mobile Android GO builds, including paths over Reticulum mesh. Exact features depend on your app version. Prefer user-owned mesh and Qortal-native tools when grids are unreliable.

Also asked as: Qortal voice · calls on GO · mesh calls

chunks.title: What should I publish in my first week?
chunks.text:
## Q: What should I publish in my first week?

A: Something lasting under your name: a small website via Web Builder, a file on Q-Share, a video, or a short document. Lasting publishes make you visible to potential nominators more than lurking alone. Also use Q-Chat so humans meet you.

Also asked as: first publish · be visible for nomination

chunks.title: What does "blocks-minted increasing" mean?
chunks.text:
## Q: What does "blocks-minted increasing" mean?

A: It is a practical health check: your minting account's count of blocks participated in should rise while you are online and approved. If it stalls for a long synced period, re-check minting key status, group membership, and Core health.

Also asked as: minting progress metric · blocks minted counter

chunks.title: Why monitor disk space on a node?
chunks.text:
## Q: Why monitor disk space on a node?

A: A full disk can halt Core, break sync, stop serving QDN, and interrupt minting. Chain + followed content grows. Leave headroom, prefer SSD, and expand storage before you hit zero bytes free.

Also asked as: disk full node · storage monitoring

chunks.title: Linux, Windows, or macOS for Core?
chunks.text:
## Q: Linux, Windows, or macOS for Core?

A: Qortal Core runs on Linux, Windows, and macOS. Many dedicated minters prefer Linux on a Pi or small PC for 24/7 uptime. Choose what you can keep updated and powered; the network does not require a data-center OS.

Also asked as: supported operating systems · run Core on Windows

chunks.title: Can names be traded?
chunks.text:
## Q: Can names be traded?

A: Yes. Names are unique and tradeable on-chain. Because QDN update rights follow the name owner, buying a name means buying control of future publishes at those coordinates. Escrow carefully and verify the name string.

Also asked as: buy a name from someone · name marketplace

chunks.title: Where do fees go?
chunks.text:
## Q: Where do fees go?

A: Fees enrich the minters keeping the network alive — not a company treasury skimming a platform cut. That design ties usage costs back to the people running infrastructure.

Also asked as: fee distribution · who gets fees

chunks.title: Why hold about 4 QORT for chat?
chunks.text:
## Q: Why hold about 4 QORT for chat?

A: Community docs describe needing around 4 QORT held (not spent) before posting freely on Q-Chat — an anti-spam gate against empty bot accounts. The coins stay yours; they are a threshold, not a chat ticket price.

Also asked as: chat balance requirement · anti spam QORT

chunks.title: About how much QORT to register a name?
chunks.text:
## Q: About how much QORT to register a name?

A: Community onboarding materials have described on the order of about 2 QORT to register a name and then additional QORT (around 4) for comfortable messaging/transactions — exact fees can change with network parameters, so confirm in your Hub UI before sending.

Also asked as: name fee amount · onboarding QORT amounts

chunks.title: What does "paid in time, for time" mean?
chunks.text:
## Q: What does "paid in time, for time" mean?

A: A community phrase meaning QORT issuance pays people for the time they keep the network secured, not for capital spent on mining rigs. Your standing grows with synchronized contribution, not with buying hashpower.

Also asked as: time for time · paid for uptime

chunks.title: Does Level 0 earn rewards?
chunks.text:
## Q: Does Level 0 earn rewards?

A: No. Level 0 earns nothing from the block reward share — it is the waiting room until you reach Level 1 after roughly 7,200 online blocks.

Also asked as: level 0 rewards · earn at level zero

chunks.title: What is a peer in Qortal?
chunks.text:
## Q: What is a peer in Qortal?

A: A peer is another node on the P2P network you sync chain data and QDN content with. More healthy peers generally mean better sync and fetch reliability. Port forwarding can help others reach you.

Also asked as: P2P peers · what are peers

chunks.title: Can I sync from any reachable peer?
chunks.text:
## Q: Can I sync from any reachable peer?

A: Yes. Nodes sync the chain from reachable peers. In restricted networks, any working peer path helps — including community-operated links. Your local copy of the chain is what keeps you independent once synced.

Also asked as: sync source · any peer sync

chunks.title: Is Qortino part of Qortal?
chunks.text:
## Q: Is Qortino part of Qortal?

A: Qortino is the offline AI companion living inside Qortal Hub / Qortal GO on your device. It can use Qortino’s on-device knowledge and, when enabled, live QDN scans from your node. It is not a cloud chatbot — answers stay on this phone.

Also asked as: what is Qortino · on-device AI

chunks.title: How should Qortino talk about Qortal?
chunks.text:
## Q: How should Qortino talk about Qortal?

A: Warm, practical, accurate: explain the network (blockchain, QDN, minting, QORT). Do not mention "game" when explaining Qortal. Only discuss Playing Qortal or Simon James if the user asked about them. Stay offline-safe; prefer metric units and short steps.

Also asked as: Qortino Qortal answers · how to explain Qortal

chunks.title: What does "latest publish wins" mean?
chunks.text:
## Q: What does "latest publish wins" mean?

A: For a given name + service + identifier triple, the newest successful publish is what fetchers retrieve. There is not a forever version museum unless an app deliberately versions identifiers (v1, v2).

Also asked as: QDN versioning · overwrite semantics

chunks.title: What is a flat dist zip?
chunks.text:
## Q: What is a flat dist zip?

A: Production Q-Apps should zip a flat build where index.html sits at the archive root, not nested in an extra folder. Nested zips cause Hub to miss index.html and show blank apps.

Also asked as: zip layout · index.html at root

chunks.title: Can I rely on npm CDNs in a Q-App?
chunks.text:
## Q: Can I rely on npm CDNs in a Q-App?

A: Avoid them. Offline users, CSP, and sovereignty goals break when apps call corporate CDNs. Vendor libraries into the zip instead.

Also asked as: CDN in Q-App · external scripts

chunks.title: Why create LTC with the account?
chunks.text:
## Q: Why create LTC with the account?

A: Community onboarding commonly auto-creates a Litecoin wallet with your Qortal account to make LTC↔QORT trading practical for newcomers. Back up whatever seed/keys that wallet uses with the same seriousness as Qortal.

Also asked as: automatic Litecoin wallet · LTC bootstrap

chunks.title: What is an unconfirmed chat message?
chunks.text:
## Q: What is an unconfirmed chat message?

A: Q-Chat uses unconfirmed transactions: messages propagate without being permanent fee-paying chain records, expire in about a day, and stay fee-free. That keeps chat light and spam-resistant when combined with the balance gate.

Also asked as: unconfirmed chat messages

chunks.title: Raspberry Pi node tips?
chunks.text:
## Q: Raspberry Pi node tips?

A: Use Pi 4/5 class with 4+ GB RAM, boot/store on SSD rather than a tiny slow SD card when possible, keep good power (UPS helps), follow your own name, and place it on stable networking. Java Core is comfortable on that class of hardware for many minters.

Also asked as: Pi 4 Qortal tips · SSD not SD card

chunks.title: What is node hygiene?
chunks.text:
## Q: What is node hygiene?

A: Keep Core updated, back up seeds offline, monitor disk, confirm minting activity if you mint, and maintain sane peer connectivity. A neglected node eventually fails at the worst time — usually during sync catch-up after a long sleep.

Also asked as: maintain a node · node checklist

chunks.title: Can non-minters use Qortal fully?
chunks.text:
## Q: Can non-minters use Qortal fully?

A: Yes. Minting is optional. Non-minters can hold QORT, register names, publish QDN content, chat, trade, and run apps. Minting is how you earn issuance and deepen governance weight — not a ticket required for basic use.

Also asked as: use without minting · non minter features

chunks.title: What is LIST service on QDN?
chunks.text:
## Q: What is LIST service on QDN?

A: LIST is a QDN service type used for list-structured resources in the ecosystem. Like other services, it is addressed by name + service + optional identifier and hosted by followers of that name. Validate formats in apps that consume lists.

Also asked as: QDN LIST · list resources

chunks.title: What is NFT on QDN?
chunks.text:
## Q: What is NFT on QDN?

A: NFT appears as a QDN service type for non-fungible style resources published under names. As always, ownership/update rights follow the registered name's owner, and data availability depends on followers hosting the payload.

Also asked as: Qortal NFT · NFT service

chunks.title: What is CODE service?
chunks.text:
## Q: What is CODE service?

A: CODE is a QDN service type for publishing code artifacts under a name. Use clear identifiers and remember that republishing the same coordinates overwrites. Consumers should still verify what they run — permissionless publish means caveat emptor.

Also asked as: publish code QDN · CODE resource

chunks.title: What is MESSAGE vs CHAIN_COMMENT?
chunks.text:
## Q: What is MESSAGE vs CHAIN_COMMENT?

A: MESSAGE is a QDN-oriented message resource type; CHAIN_COMMENT is a tiny fully on-chain 239-byte comment. Use CHAIN_COMMENT for microscopic permanent anchors; use broader message/mail/document services when you need more space or encryption features.

Also asked as: MESSAGE service · comment types

chunks.title: What is window._qdnTheme?
chunks.text:
## Q: What is window._qdnTheme?

A: Hub injects host variables into Q-Apps such as window._qdnTheme (light|dark) and window._qdnContext (e.g. gateway). Apps can theme themselves to match Hub without calling a cloud. Feature-detect qortalRequest before assuming wallet APIs exist.

Also asked as: Q-App theme variable · _qdnContext

chunks.title: What is exqlorer?
chunks.text:
## Q: What is exqlorer?

A: Community materials mention block explorers such as exqlorer.com for viewing live chain figures like current block reward. When you are offline, rely on your local node's block info and apps like Q-Minter instead of assuming a website is reachable.

Also asked as: block explorer · check block reward

chunks.title: What is #QQQ?
chunks.text:
## Q: What is #QQQ?

A: In Playing Qortal community language, #QQQ refers to circulating QORT as money inside real human circles — paying friends and local trade in QORT as the practice spreads. It is cultural usage around the coin, not a second token.

Also asked as: QQQ meaning · pay in QORT locally

chunks.title: How many Minter Admins are there?
chunks.text:
## Q: How many Minter Admins are there?

A: Counts change as the community elects people. Older snapshots mentioned around 21 Minter Admins with approval needing on the order of ~40% of signatures — treat numbers as snapshots, not eternal constants. What stays true: shared on-chain approval, not one person's private switch.

Also asked as: admin count · how many signatures for minting

chunks.title: What is the address letter Q for?
chunks.text:
## Q: What is the address letter Q for?

A: It is simply the visible prefix of Qortal addresses — a quick sanity check you are copying a Qortal address and not another chain's format. Always verify the full string, not only the first character.

Also asked as: why addresses start with Q

chunks.title: What does "no yearly renewal" mean for names?
chunks.text:
## Q: What does "no yearly renewal" mean for names?

A: There is no ICANN-style registrar charging you every year to keep the name. Ownership is on-chain with your account until you transfer it. The real renewal risk is losing your seedphrase.

Also asked as: name registrar · keep name forever

chunks.title: Can I have multiple registered names?
chunks.text:
## Q: Can I have multiple registered names?

A: Accounts can own more than one name if you register or acquire them. Each name is its own QDN publishing root. Remember fees and the responsibility of backing up the single seed that controls them all.

Also asked as: many names one account · secondary name

chunks.title: What is GET_ACCOUNT_NAMES for?
chunks.text:
## Q: What is GET_ACCOUNT_NAMES for?

A: In Q-Apps, GET_ACCOUNT_NAMES retrieves the registered names for an address via qortalRequest. Useful after GET_USER_ACCOUNT when an app needs to know which name to publish under.

Also asked as: list names for address

chunks.title: Why chunk large files?
chunks.text:
## Q: Why chunk large files?

A: Huge payloads are awkward for some services and UX. Prefer FILE service and sensible chunking/packaging rather than stuffing oversized data into DOCUMENT. Users on modest nodes will thank you.

Also asked as: large file publishing · chunk uploads

chunks.title: What is GIF_REPOSITORY?
chunks.text:
## Q: What is GIF_REPOSITORY?

A: It is a multi-file QDN service pattern (alongside WEBSITE/APP) for gif repositories. Fetching needs filepath semantics like other multi-file resources. Publish via flows your Hub version supports for multi-file packages.

Also asked as: gif repository service

chunks.title: What is BLOG_COMMENT?
chunks.text:
## Q: What is BLOG_COMMENT?

A: BLOG_COMMENT is a QDN service used by blogging apps for comments threaded to posts. Comments are still resources under names/services/identifiers — validate them in apps like any other permissionless data.

Also asked as: blog comments QDN

chunks.title: How do I version QDN data without losing history?
chunks.text:
## Q: How do I version QDN data without losing history?

A: Use new identifiers for immutable versions (myapp_post_2026_01_a) and optionally a mutable pointer identifier for "latest". Overwriting the same identifier replaces history at that coordinate.

Also asked as: immutable identifiers · version pointer

chunks.title: What is DECRYPT_DATA used for?
chunks.text:
## Q: What is DECRYPT_DATA used for?

A: Q-Apps use decryption actions (such as DECRYPT_DATA or group variants) via qortalRequest so the wallet can decrypt private QDN payloads for the logged-in user. Private services are useless without the recipient key.

Also asked as: decrypt private QDN · wallet decrypt

chunks.title: Why feature-detect qortalRequest?
chunks.text:
## Q: Why feature-detect qortalRequest?

A: Pages may open outside Hub/GO (previews, browsers) where the bridge is missing. Resolve window.qortalRequest or parent/top, and show a clear message to open inside Hub/GO instead of crashing.

Also asked as: qortalRequest missing · open inside Hub

chunks.title: Why set Vite base to ./ ?
chunks.text:
## Q: Why set Vite base to ./ ?

A: Relative base paths make asset URLs work when Hub serves the app from a nested render path. Absolute roots often 404 inside QDN rendering. Rebuild after changing base.

Also asked as: Vite base path · relative assets

chunks.title: What is the trailing slash SPA issue?
chunks.text:
## Q: What is the trailing slash SPA issue?

A: If Hub opens /render/APP/YourName without a trailing slash, relative ./assets/file.js may resolve against /render/APP/ and 404. Fixes include ensuring a trailing slash, a correct base href, or paths that match how Hub serves you.

Also asked as: render path slash · relative URL bug

chunks.title: What is IMAGE_PRIVATE?
chunks.text:
## Q: What is IMAGE_PRIVATE?

A: A private image service variant encrypted for a recipient. Only their key decrypts it. Use when a public IMAGE would leak the photo to anyone who fetches the coordinates.

Also asked as: private image QDN

chunks.title: What is MAIL_PRIVATE?
chunks.text:
## Q: What is MAIL_PRIVATE?

A: Encrypted mail-style QDN data for a recipient. It is the private counterpart to mail publishing — confidentiality depends on cryptography and key custody, not on hiding an identifier.

Also asked as: private Q-Mail resource

chunks.title: How do thumbs differ from images?
chunks.text:
## Q: How do thumbs differ from images?

A: THUMBNAIL (~500 KB) is for small previews/avatars; IMAGE (~10 MB) is for fuller pictures. Using IMAGE for avatars wastes bandwidth; using THUMBNAIL for large photos will fail limits.

Also asked as: thumbnail vs image · avatar size limit

chunks.title: Can ARRR be traded on the Trade Portal?
chunks.text:
## Q: Can ARRR be traded on the Trade Portal?

A: Yes — Pirate Chain (ARRR) is among the coins listed for Trade Portal AT trading alongside LTC, BTC, DOGE, RVN, and DGB. Availability of specific offers depends on peers posting trades.

Also asked as: Pirate Chain trade · ARRR QORT

chunks.title: Can DOGE be traded for QORT?
chunks.text:
## Q: Can DOGE be traded for QORT?

A: Yes. DOGE is listed among Trade Portal cross-chain AT trade coins. You need a workable DOGE path and an open peer offer; there is no custodial dogecoin company desk inside Qortal.

Also asked as: DOGE to QORT · Dogecoin trade

chunks.title: Can RVN be traded?
chunks.text:
## Q: Can RVN be traded?

A: Yes. Ravencoin (RVN) is among supported Trade Portal AT trade coins. Peer offers set the price; verify amounts and fees before you commit.

Also asked as: Ravencoin trade · RVN QORT

chunks.title: Can DGB be traded?
chunks.text:
## Q: Can DGB be traded?

A: Yes. DigiByte (DGB) appears in the Trade Portal coin list for AT trades with QORT. As with all pairs, success depends on open offers and correct wallet handling on both sides.

Also asked as: DigiByte trade · DGB QORT

chunks.title: Can I run a node on a laptop?
chunks.text:
## Q: Can I run a node on a laptop?

A: Yes, but laptops sleep and travel — uptime suffers for minting. Fine for learning and light use; for serious minting, a small always-on box is happier.

Also asked as: laptop node · notebook minting

chunks.title: How much water should I store per person per day?
chunks.text:
## Q: How much water should I store per person per day?

A: Plan at least 4 litres per person per day: about 2 for drinking and 2 for cooking and basic hygiene. In heat, hard work, illness, or pregnancy, drinking alone can need 4–6 litres. Two weeks per person is a solid household baseline — a family of four needs roughly 112 litres for one week.

Also asked as: daily water needs emergency · how much water to store · water storage amount

chunks.title: How do I store water safely at home?
chunks.text:
## Q: How do I store water safely at home?

A: Use food-grade containers only (HDPE #2 jugs, 200 L drums, or factory-sealed bottled water). Store cool and dark, off concrete on wood slats. Never reuse milk jugs. Tap water from a treated municipal supply can store as-is; rotate yearly. For well water, add 2 drops of unscented 5–6% bleach per litre when filling.

Also asked as: water storage containers · how to store drinking water · emergency water storage

chunks.title: How do I purify water by boiling?
chunks.text:
## Q: How do I purify water by boiling?

A: 1. Bring water to a rolling boil.
2. Keep it boiling 1 minute (3 minutes above about 2,000 m elevation).
3. Let it cool covered before drinking.
Boiling kills bacteria, protozoa, and viruses — the gold standard when you have fuel.
Do NOT skip the full boil time at altitude, where water boils cooler.

Also asked as: boil water to make safe · rolling boil water treatment · how long to boil water · how do I make water safe to drink · make water safe to drink · how to purify drinking water

chunks.title: How do I treat water with household bleach?
chunks.text:
## Q: How do I treat water with household bleach?

A: 1. Use unscented 5–6% household bleach only.
2. Add 2 drops per litre of clear water, or 4 drops per litre if cloudy (after settling/pre-filtering).
3. Mix and wait 30–60 minutes before drinking.
Bleach helps against bacteria and viruses but is only partial against Cryptosporidium.
Do NOT use scented, colour-safe, or cleaning blends — only plain bleach.

Also asked as: bleach water purification · chlorine drops for drinking water · disinfect water with bleach · how do I purify water with bleach · purify water with bleach · bleach to make water safe

chunks.title: Do hollow-fiber water filters remove viruses?
chunks.text:
## Q: Do hollow-fiber water filters remove viruses?

A: A good hollow-fiber filter (about 0.1 micron) removes bacteria and protozoa (Giardia/Crypto) but typically does NOT remove viruses. Pair it with boiling or a chemical that covers viruses (chlorine dioxide or bleach for many viruses), or use a true purifier bottle. Protect hollow-fiber filters from freezing — cracked fibres can pass microbes with no visible damage. With no fire: filter first, then use chemical treatment or a purifier — do not rely on clear looks alone.

Also asked as: Sawyer filter viruses · 0.1 micron filter what it removes · does a water filter kill viruses · how do I filter river water · filter river water · what if I have no fire to boil water

chunks.title: What is the best layered water treatment kit?
chunks.text:
## Q: What is the best layered water treatment kit?

A: Cover three layers: a gravity or squeeze hollow-fiber filter for volume, chlorine dioxide tablets as compact backup (best chemical option; wait up to 4 hours for Crypto), and the knowledge plus fuel to boil. Mark dedicated dirty and clean buckets permanently to avoid cross-contamination.

Also asked as: water purification toolkit · three ways to purify water · home water treatment layers

chunks.title: How do I make muddy river water drinkable?
chunks.text:
## Q: How do I make muddy river water drinkable?

A: 1. Pre-filter through cloth, a coffee filter, or a Millbank bag, or let sediment settle and decant.
2. Then boil, filter with a hollow-fiber unit, and/or use chlorine dioxide.
3. Prefer moving water, collected from the surface upstream of trails and livestock.
Sediment shelters microbes and clogs filters.
Do NOT drink untreated surface water no matter how clear — Giardia is invisible.

Also asked as: cloudy water purification · pre-filter dirty water · treat lake or stream water

chunks.title: Can I drink rainwater from my roof?
chunks.text:
## Q: Can I drink rainwater from my roof?

A: Rain catchment is useful: roughly 1 litre per square metre per millimetre of rain (a 20 m² roof in a 10 mm shower ≈ 200 L). First-flush the initial runoff that carries roof grime and bird droppings, then still treat before drinking (boil, filter, or chemical). Use clean tarp or metal roof sections into food-grade barrels.

Also asked as: rain catchment drinking · is rainwater safe to drink · collect rain for drinking · can I drink rainwater · is rain water drinkable

chunks.title: Is urine or salt water drinkable in survival?
chunks.text:
## Q: Is urine or salt water drinkable in survival?

A: Salt water and urine are never drinkable as-is — both dehydrate you further. Distillation is the only practical way to reclaim usable water from them. Focus on finding fresh sources, melting snow properly, rain catchment, or treating surface water instead.

Also asked as: can I drink urine · drink seawater survival · urine as water source

chunks.title: How do I get water from snow or ice?
chunks.text:
## Q: How do I get water from snow or ice?

A: Melt snow with a little starter liquid in the pot so it does not scorch. Ice yields more water per volume than snow. In cold conditions, never eat snow directly — it lowers core temperature. Once melted, treat as needed (boil is most reliable). Keep hollow-fiber filters warm against your body so they do not freeze.

Also asked as: melt snow for drinking · winter water survival · eat snow for hydration

chunks.title: Should I ration water in the heat?
chunks.text:
## Q: Should I ration water in the heat?

A: Ration sweat, not water: rest in shade through midday, work at dawn and dusk, and drink what you have. People have died of dehydration with water still in their canteens. Shade, pacing, and treating every available source beat sipping tiny amounts while still sweating hard.

Also asked as: ration water desert · drink or save water survival · dehydration with water left

chunks.title: How do chlorine dioxide tablets compare to bleach?
chunks.text:
## Q: How do chlorine dioxide tablets compare to bleach?

A: Chlorine dioxide tablets are the best chemical option for field use: they cover bacteria, viruses, and Cryptosporidium (often needing up to about 4 hours for Crypto). Bleach is cheap and common but only partial against Crypto. Keep tablets as compact backup even if you mainly boil or filter.

Also asked as: chlorine dioxide vs bleach · best chemical water treatment · water tablets Crypto

chunks.title: What water sources should I prefer in the wild?
chunks.text:
## Q: What water sources should I prefer in the wild?

A: Prefer moving water over stagnant. Collect from the surface, not a stirred-up bottom, and upstream of trails, livestock, and settlements. Always treat before drinking. Avoid salt water and anything you cannot distill. Clarity means nothing — treat every wild source.

Also asked as: best wild water source · stream vs puddle drinking · where to collect water outdoors

chunks.title: How do I protect a water filter in winter?
chunks.text:
## Q: How do I protect a water filter in winter?

A: Freezing destroys hollow-fiber filters — cracked fibres can pass microbes with no visible damage. Sleep with the filter in your jacket, keep it against your body when hiking, or switch to boiling and chemicals in hard freezes. Never assume a thawed filter is still safe if it froze solid.

Also asked as: freeze Sawyer filter · winter water filter care · hollow fiber freezing

chunks.title: What elevation changes boiling time for water?
chunks.text:
## Q: What elevation changes boiling time for water?

A: At low elevation, a rolling boil for 1 minute is the usual standard. Above about 2,000 m, boil 3 minutes because water boils at a lower temperature. When fuel is scarce, a quality filter plus chemical backup can save fuel, but boiling remains the most foolproof microbial kill.

Also asked as: boil water altitude · 2000 m boil longer · high elevation water treatment

chunks.title: What is the survival rule of threes?
chunks.text:
## Q: What is the survival rule of threes?

A: Rough priorities: about 3 minutes without air, 3 hours without shelter in harsh exposure, 3 days without water, and 3 weeks without food. In cold, wet climates, shelter and fire often outrank everything else — hypothermia kills far faster than hunger.

Also asked as: rule of threes survival · 3 minutes 3 hours 3 days · survival priorities order

chunks.title: What are the 5 C's of survivability?
chunks.text:
## Q: What are the 5 C's of survivability?

A: A common bushcraft framework: (1) Cutting tool — fixed-blade knife; (2) Combustion — ferro rod, lighter, tinder; (3) Cover — tarp/blanket/rain gear; (4) Container — metal bottle or pot you can boil in; (5) Cordage — paracord or bankline. These are hard to improvise well in the field.

Also asked as: five Cs bushcraft · Dave Canterbury 5 Cs · what to carry survival kit

chunks.title: How do I build a reliable fire in the wild?
chunks.text:
## Q: How do I build a reliable fire in the wild?

A: 1. Gather tinder, pencil-thin twigs, then finger- and wrist-thick fuel before striking.
2. Build on dry ground or a stick platform; shield from wind.
3. Light the tinder, then feed gradually up in size.
Carry two ignition sources; a ferro rod still works when wet/cold lighters fail.
Do NOT light first and scramble for fuel — that is how fires die.

Also asked as: how to start a campfire · fire lay tinder kindling · make fire survival · how do I start a fire without matches · start fire without matches · fire with ferro rod

chunks.title: How do I make fire in winter snow?
chunks.text:
## Q: How do I make fire in winter snow?

A: Clear snow to ground or build a raft of green logs so the fire does not melt into a pit. Use standing dead wood (ground wood is soaked), split to dry cores, and process 3–4× more fuel than feels necessary before lighting. Feather sticks and fatwood light when everything else is wet. Warm the ferro rod and your hands first.

Also asked as: winter fire starting · fire on snow · wet wood fire tips

chunks.title: How should I site and build an emergency shelter?
chunks.text:
## Q: How should I site and build an emergency shelter?

A: 1. Pick a site out of wind, off low ground, away from dead standing trees.
2. Rig a tarp A-frame or lean-to fast.
3. Insulate underneath you — ground conduction steals more heat than air.
A quality emergency blanket or wool layer under/over you matters as much as the roof.
Do NOT soak your clothes with sweat while overbuilding a debris hut in cold weather.

Also asked as: emergency shelter site · tarp A-frame lean-to · where to build shelter · how do I build a shelter outside · build outdoor shelter · emergency shelter outside · how to make a shelter outdoors

chunks.title: Why is wool better than cotton in the cold?
chunks.text:
## Q: Why is wool better than cotton in the cold?

A: Never wear cotton against skin when cold — it holds moisture and chills you. Wool (and many synthetics) insulates even when wet; down fails when wet. Wool also resists ember burns near fires and odour over multi-day wear. A sturdy wool blanket can serve as coat, sleep system, stretcher pad, or windbreak.

Also asked as: wool vs cotton survival · cotton kills myth · best fabric cold wet

chunks.title: How do I signal for help if I am lost?
chunks.text:
## Q: How do I signal for help if I am lost?

A: 1. Stop, stay warm, and stay put if safe.
2. Make yourself visible: open ground, bright colours, signal mirror/flashes.
3. Use three of anything — whistle blasts, fires, or light flashes — as a distress pattern.
A whistle carries farther than shouting for far less energy.
Do NOT wander farther looking for a perfect ridge once you are already exhausted and cold.

Also asked as: distress signal three fires · whistle survival signal · how to signal rescuers

chunks.title: How do I navigate without a GPS?
chunks.text:
## Q: How do I navigate without a GPS?

A: Carry a compass and paper map even if you have GPS. Without a compass: sun rises roughly east and sets roughly west; a stick’s shadow tip marked twice gives an east–west line; the North Star (via the Big Dipper pointers) sits due north. Pace-count distance (calibrate your own paces; many adults are ~65 double-paces per 100 m). Look behind you regularly so the return route is memorised.

Also asked as: compass and map basics · primitive navigation sun · find north without compass

chunks.title: What should I do if I get lost outdoors?
chunks.text:
## Q: What should I do if I get lost outdoors?

A: 1. Stop. Sit, breathe, and prevent panic decisions.
2. Stay warm and dry — shelter and fire before long searches.
3. Mark your location, make yourself visible, and signal (whistle threes).
Tell someone your route and return time before you leave home.
Do NOT keep walking for hours hoping to stumble on a road when night and cold are coming.

Also asked as: lost in woods what to do · STOP method survival · I'm lost hiking

chunks.title: How does ground insulation affect shelter warmth?
chunks.text:
## Q: How does ground insulation affect shelter warmth?

A: You lose more heat into the ground than into the air. Always put insulation under you: closed-cell foam, a thick bed of dry debris, packs, or extra clothing. A tarp roof without under-insulation still leaves you cold. Elevate or pad before you add fancy walls.

Also asked as: sleeping on cold ground · ground conduction heat loss · insulate under sleeping bag

chunks.title: How do I gather fuel before lighting a fire?
chunks.text:
## Q: How do I gather fuel before lighting a fire?

A: Collect the whole ladder first: fluffy or bark tinder, pencil-thin twigs, finger-thick sticks, then wrist-thick fuel. Light only when the pile is ready and weather-protected. Leaving a baby flame to fetch wood is a classic way to lose the fire — especially in winter.

Also asked as: firewood sizes tinder kindling · stages of fire fuel · prepare fire materials

chunks.title: What ignition sources should I carry?
chunks.text:
## Q: What ignition sources should I carry?

A: Carry at least two ignition sources. A butane lighter is convenient; a ferro rod still throws sparks when wet or frozen. Pair both with dry tinder on your body. Bic-style lighters fail in cold until warmed in a pocket.

Also asked as: ferro rod vs lighter · two ways to make fire · backup fire starter

chunks.title: How do I use a tarp as a quick shelter?
chunks.text:
## Q: How do I use a tarp as a quick shelter?

A: An A-frame or lean-to tarp is the fastest effective shelter for most people. Rig ridge line with cordage, stake corners, and put thick insulation on the ground under your sleep system. Face the open side away from wind and rain. Practice at home so you can do it in the dark.

Also asked as: tarp A-frame shelter · lean-to tarp setup · emergency tarp camping

chunks.title: What does three whistle blasts mean?
chunks.text:
## Q: What does three whistle blasts mean?

A: Three of anything — whistle blasts, fires, or light flashes — is widely recognised as a distress signal. Carry a loud whistle; it saves voice and energy. Keep signalling on a schedule so rescuers can home in.

Also asked as: whistle three times distress · universal help signal · signal mirror three flashes

chunks.title: How should I dress in layers for cold weather?
chunks.text:
## Q: How should I dress in layers for cold weather?

A: Use a moisture-managing base (wool/synthetic, not cotton), an insulating mid layer, and a wind/rain shell. Vent before you sweat; damp clothing destroys insulation. Cover head and hands. Change into dry sleep clothes before bed in the field.

Also asked as: layering system cold · base mid outer layer · stay dry to stay warm

chunks.title: How do I avoid soaking clothes while building shelter?
chunks.text:
## Q: How do I avoid soaking clothes while building shelter?

A: Debris and snow shelters cost sweat. Vent layers, work at a sustainable pace, and stop to rewarm before you are damp. Wet clothing in wind can turn shelter-building into a hypothermia emergency. Sometimes a simple tarp beats an epic debris hut.

Also asked as: sweat hypothermia risk · slow down shelter building · stay dry working cold

chunks.title: What should I tell someone before a hike?
chunks.text:
## Q: What should I tell someone before a hike?

A: Share your route, companions, and return time with someone who will notice if you are late. Agree when they should call for help. This single habit saves more lives than exotic gear, because searchers know where to look.

Also asked as: leave trip plan · route return time hiking · tell friend before outdoors

chunks.title: What makes a fixed-blade knife the top bushcraft tool?
chunks.text:
## Q: What makes a fixed-blade knife the top bushcraft tool?

A: A decent fixed-blade carbon-steel knife processes tinder, builds shelter, prepares food, and does camp crafts when folders fail. It is the cutting tool in the 5 C’s because replacing that capability from scratch in the field is hard. Keep it sharp and sheathed.

Also asked as: best survival knife · fixed blade vs folder field · cutting tool 5 Cs

chunks.title: What wild plants are safer learning targets?
chunks.text:
## Q: What wild plants are safer learning targets?

A: Learn a handful of unmistakable local species from experts — e.g. bilberries/crowberries in some northern regions, and widespread cooked nettles or dandelion greens elsewhere. Harvest away from roads and spray. Never invent tests for unknown plants or mushrooms.

Also asked as: beginner foraging plants · nettle dandelion food · unmistakable wild edibles

chunks.title: Why shouldn't I eat unidentified mushrooms?
chunks.text:
## Q: Why shouldn't I eat unidentified mushrooms?

A: Assume any wild mushroom is unsafe until an expert confirms the exact species — there is no reliable shortcut test. Never experiment. Learn a handful of unmistakable local plants from experts and leave all uncertain fungi alone. Mistakes can be fatal.

Also asked as: wild mushroom danger · foraging mushrooms safe · mushroom identification rule

chunks.title: Why keep paper maps if I have offline map apps?
chunks.text:
## Q: Why keep paper maps if I have offline map apps?

A: Phones die, freeze, drown, and fail. A paper map with rally points marked, plus a compass you know how to use, still works. Download offline maps too — redundancy is the point. Tell someone your route before you go.

Also asked as: paper map vs phone · GPS battery dead navigation · analog navigation prep

chunks.title: How do I recognize and treat hypothermia?
chunks.text:
## Q: How do I recognize and treat hypothermia?

A: 1. Get them out of wind and wet clothing; add dry insulation.
2. If fully conscious, give warm sweet drinks; warm the torso with skin-to-skin or heat packs (not extremities first).
3. Handle gently and seek emergency services (112 in Europe) if available — severe hypothermia is life-threatening.
Early signs: intense shivering, clumsy hands, slurred speech, apathy.
Do NOT rub extremities hard, give alcohol, or use hot baths on a semi-conscious person.

Also asked as: hypothermia symptoms treatment · someone too cold shivering · field care for hypothermia

chunks.title: How do I stay warm when home heating fails?
chunks.text:
## Q: How do I stay warm when home heating fails?

A: Heat the person, then one room, then maybe the house. Wear wool/synthetic base layers, hat and warm socks indoors, use a hot water bottle in a sleeping bag, and gather everyone in the smallest sheltered room with doors closed and blankets over windows. A climate-rated sleeping bag is a heating system that needs no fuel. Safe heat: wood stove, or indoor-rated heaters with ventilation and a working CO alarm.

Also asked as: blackout heating tips · one warm room strategy · no heat winter home · how do I stay warm without power · stay warm without electricity · keep warm in a power outage · no power heating

chunks.title: What causes carbon monoxide poisoning in blackouts?
chunks.text:
## Q: What causes carbon monoxide poisoning in blackouts?

A: Carbon monoxide from combustion kills quietly every winter. Never heat or cook with a barbecue, camp stove, open oven, or generator indoors or in a garage. Generators stay outdoors, 5+ m from windows, exhaust pointed away. Indoor-rated paraffin/propane heaters still need a cracked window and a working CO alarm with fresh batteries.

Also asked as: CO poisoning generator · never run generator indoors · carbon monoxide heater danger

chunks.title: What are the signs of carbon monoxide poisoning?
chunks.text:
## Q: What are the signs of carbon monoxide poisoning?

A: 1. Headache, nausea, dizziness, confusion, or flu-like symptoms with combustion appliances running — get everyone outside to fresh air immediately.
2. Turn off the source if safe; ventilate.
3. Call emergency services if anyone is altered, fainting, or not improving.
CO is odourless.
Do NOT go back inside to "sleep it off" next to the heater or generator.

Also asked as: CO poisoning symptoms · carbon monoxide headache · feel sick with heater on

chunks.title: What light sources are best in a blackout?
chunks.text:
## Q: What light sources are best in a blackout?

A: Priority: LED headlamps (hands-free; 50–150 hours on low), then LED lanterns, then flame (candles/oil lamps) with hard rules — stable holders, away from curtains, never asleep or unattended, plus smoke alarms and an extinguisher. Prefer lithium primary AA/AAA (10–20 year shelf life); alkalines leak in storage. Add solar recharge when possible.

Also asked as: emergency lighting blackout · headlamp vs candles · best blackout lights

chunks.title: How do I handle toilet sanitation when water is out?
chunks.text:
## Q: How do I handle toilet sanitation when water is out?

A: If sewers are intact, flush manually with 6–8 L of non-potable water poured into the bowl at once. If sewage may back up or water is precious: twin buckets — urine separate; feces in a lined bucket covered with sawdust, ash, or dry soil after each use. Wash hands every time. Store sealed waste away from living areas; bury later 20+ cm deep and 60+ m from water if authorities allow.

Also asked as: toilet not flushing emergency · twin bucket toilet · sanitation grid down

chunks.title: Why is handwashing critical in disasters?
chunks.text:
## Q: Why is handwashing critical in disasters?

A: In historical grid-down events, hygiene-related illness dwarfed injury. Most disaster diseases are fecal–oral and stop at clean hands. Set a wash station (jug with tap or pierced-cap bottle, soap, towel) by the toilet bucket and kitchen. Alcohol gel (60%+) is backup, not a full substitute when hands are soiled.

Also asked as: hygiene grid down · disaster disease prevention · handwashing emergency

chunks.title: Are candles safe for blackout heat?
chunks.text:
## Q: Are candles safe for blackout heat?

A: Candles and oil lamps are for light and morale, not primary heat. Use stable holders, keep away from curtains, never leave them asleep or unattended, and keep a fire extinguisher and smoke alarm per level. Glow sticks are child-safe night lights with zero fire risk. Headlamps beat open flame for task light.

Also asked as: heating with candles · candle safety emergency · oil lamp rules

chunks.title: What batteries should I store for emergencies?
chunks.text:
## Q: What batteries should I store for emergencies?

A: Lithium primary AA/AAA cells store 10–20 years without leaking. Alkalines often leak and ruin devices in long storage. Rechargeables plus a small solar panel make light and radios self-sustaining. Standardise sizes across headlamps and radios to simplify logistics.

Also asked as: lithium vs alkaline storage · best batteries for prep · batteries that don't leak

chunks.title: How do I cool a burn in the field?
chunks.text:
## Q: How do I cool a burn in the field?

A: 1. Cool with running cool (not ice) water for 20 minutes.
2. Cover loosely with a clean non-fluffy dressing.
3. For large, deep, facial, genital, or circumferential burns — seek emergency care urgently.
This is educational first aid, not a substitute for professional care.
Do NOT apply butter, toothpaste, ice packs directly, or puncture large blisters as "treatment."

Also asked as: treat burn first aid · cool running water burn · burn dressing emergency · first aid for burns · how do I treat a burn · burn first aid

chunks.title: What is the one-warm-room strategy?
chunks.text:
## Q: What is the one-warm-room strategy?

A: Pick the smallest room on the sheltered side of the house, close doors, hang blankets over doorways and windows, and gather people, pets, and safe light sources there. Body heat alone can hold a small sealed room several degrees above the rest of the house. Sleep in bags rated for your climate.

Also asked as: seal one room blackout · body heat warm room · blanket over windows heat

chunks.title: Can I heat my house with a charcoal barbecue indoors?
chunks.text:
## Q: Can I heat my house with a charcoal barbecue indoors?

A: Never. Barbecues, camp stoves, ovens left open, and generators used indoors produce carbon monoxide that kills without a strong smell warning. Only use heating appliances rated for indoor use, with ventilation and a working CO alarm. When in doubt, add clothing and sleeping bags instead of burning fuel inside.

Also asked as: BBQ indoors heating · grill inside garage winter · charcoal carbon monoxide

chunks.title: How do I set up an emergency handwashing station?
chunks.text:
## Q: How do I set up an emergency handwashing station?

A: Place a jug with a tap or a bottle with a pierced cap, soap, and a towel beside the toilet bucket and the kitchen. Make handwashing automatic after toilet use and before food. Alcohol gel (60%+) backs it up when water is scarce but does not remove heavy soil alone.

Also asked as: tippy tap emergency · handwash jug soap · sanitation wash station

chunks.title: What is the twin-bucket toilet system?
chunks.text:
## Q: What is the twin-bucket toilet system?

A: One bucket for urine (lower hazard; dilute and dispose away from water). One lined bucket for feces, covered after each use with sawdust, ash, dry soil, or shredded paper to control odour and flies. Seal, store away from living space, wash hands every time. This prevents disease when toilets fail.

Also asked as: two bucket sanitation · urine feces separate · emergency loo sawdust

chunks.title: How do I manually flush a toilet with no water service?
chunks.text:
## Q: How do I manually flush a toilet with no water service?

A: If sewer lines are intact, pour 6–8 litres of non-potable water (rain, pool, ditch) into the bowl in one confident pour to siphon-flush. Do not waste drinking water on this if sewers may back up — switch to the twin-bucket system instead.

Also asked as: pour flush toilet · bucket flush litres · toilet works no water

chunks.title: How do I safely use an indoor-rated propane heater?
chunks.text:
## Q: How do I safely use an indoor-rated propane heater?

A: Only use heaters explicitly rated for indoor use. Crack a window for oxygen, keep a working carbon-monoxide alarm with fresh batteries, and follow clearances from walls and bedding. If anyone feels headache or nausea, shut it down and get to fresh air — then reassess.

Also asked as: catalytic heater ventilation · kerosene heater CO alarm · indoor heater rules

chunks.title: Why avoid cotton base layers when cold and wet?
chunks.text:
## Q: Why avoid cotton base layers when cold and wet?

A: Cotton holds water against skin and accelerates heat loss — a fast path toward hypothermia in wind. Choose wool or synthetics next to skin for cold weather work and sleep systems. Save cotton for hot, dry chores if you must.

Also asked as: cotton kills saying · wet cotton hypothermia · synthetic base layer

chunks.title: What should still work with no electricity at all?
chunks.text:
## Q: What should still work with no electricity at all?

A: Shrink true power needs to refrigeration, communications, light, and medical devices. Fallbacks: wool blankets and climate-rated sleeping bags, headlamps with lithium primaries, candles/oil lamp, thermos, hand-crank radio, paper maps, printed contacts/manuals, books and games. Power plans fail less when survival does not depend on every gadget.

Also asked as: unplugged baseline preps · non electric survival gear · live without power

chunks.title: How often should I rotate stored water and bleach?
chunks.text:
## Q: How often should I rotate stored water and bleach?

A: Rotate stored municipal water about yearly; refresh well water treatment when refilling. Rotate unscented bleach about yearly because it loses strength. Date containers with a marker so the future you does not guess.

Also asked as: rotate water yearly · bleach rotation prep · water storage maintenance

chunks.title: How do I treat heat illness in the field?
chunks.text:
## Q: How do I treat heat illness in the field?

A: 1. Stop activity; move to shade or a cool place.
2. Loosen clothing; cool with wet cloths; sip safe fluids with electrolytes if available.
3. If confused, fainting, or extremely hot skin — this can be life-threatening: cool aggressively and seek emergency services if reachable.
Do NOT force someone who is confused to drink large amounts, and do not keep working through severe symptoms.

Also asked as: heat exhaustion field · too hot stop work · shade rest drink

chunks.title: How do I stop severe bleeding?
chunks.text:
## Q: How do I stop severe bleeding?

A: 1. Apply hard direct pressure on the wound with the cleanest cloth available — do not peek repeatedly.
2. Elevate if practical; keep pressing.
3. Use a commercial tourniquet high and tight only for life-threatening limb bleeding that pressure cannot stop; note the time.
Call emergency services (112 in Europe) if reachable — uncontrolled bleeding is a life threat.
Do NOT loosen a tourniquet every few minutes "to check."

Also asked as: severe bleeding first aid · direct pressure wound · tourniquet when to use

chunks.title: How do I clean and dress a cut when no clinic is available?
chunks.text:
## Q: How do I clean and dress a cut when no clinic is available?

A: 1. Irrigate thoroughly with drinkable water under pressure; remove debris.
2. Dress with clean gauze; change daily.
3. Watch for spreading redness, heat, swelling, pus, red streaks, or fever — those need professional care urgently.
Training beats gear; take a first-aid course before you need it.
Do NOT pack dirt, ash, or unproven home pastes into a deep wound.

Also asked as: treat wound off grid · irrigate cut clean water · infection signs wound

chunks.title: What should be in a home first-aid kit?
chunks.text:
## Q: What should be in a home first-aid kit?

A: Layer it: boo-boo (bandages, blister plasters, antiseptic, tweezers, tape), wound (gauze, elastic bandages, gloves, irrigation syringe, triangular bandages), trauma if trained (pressure bandage, hemostatic gauze, commercial tourniquet, chest seal, space blankets), plus oral rehydration salts, thermometer, and your usual medicines rotated. Personal prescriptions with the largest lawful buffer matter most in long disruptions.

Also asked as: emergency first aid kit list · trauma kit layers · home medical supplies prep

chunks.title: How do I make oral rehydration solution?
chunks.text:
## Q: How do I make oral rehydration solution?

A: For adult or child diarrhea/vomiting when dehydration is the risk: mix 1 litre of safe water + 6 level teaspoons sugar + ½ level teaspoon salt; sip constantly. Continue feeding children. Seek emergency or clinical care if reachable for severe dehydration, bloody stool, or a floppy/lethargic child. Hand and water hygiene protect the rest of the household.

Also asked as: ORS recipe WHO · diarrhea dehydration treatment · homemade electrolyte drink · how do I treat dehydration · how to treat dehydration · dehydration treatment · how do I rehydrate · treat dehydration at home

chunks.title: How do I remove a tick safely?
chunks.text:
## Q: How do I remove a tick safely?

A: 1. Grip with fine tweezers at the skin; pull steady and straight — no twisting or burning.
2. Disinfect the site; note the date.
3. Watch weeks for expanding rash or flu-like symptoms and seek medical attention if they appear.
Check skin after walks in forest, brush, or tall grass.
Do NOT smother with oil, burn, or jerk the body so the mouthparts snap off deeper.

Also asked as: tick bite what to do · remove tick tweezers · tick first aid

chunks.title: What is the priority order for medical preparedness?
chunks.text:
## Q: What is the priority order for medical preparedness?

A: Training beats gear: certified first-aid/CPR first, wilderness first aid if you go remote, then equipment. An untrained person with a full trauma kit is less capable than a trained one with a bandana. Practice under supervision; in real emergencies contact emergency services if at all possible.

Also asked as: first aid training vs gear · CPR course preparedness · skills before trauma kit

chunks.title: What hygiene rules prevent foodborne illness off-grid?
chunks.text:
## Q: What hygiene rules prevent foodborne illness off-grid?

A: Cook thoroughly, keep raw and cooked separate, and do not leave perishable leftovers at room temperature beyond about 2 hours. Pair that with handwashing and safe water. In every prolonged disruption, sanitation and food hygiene prevent more misery than bandages.

Also asked as: safe food handling emergency · cook thoroughly leftovers · kitchen hygiene blackout

chunks.title: What belongs in the trauma layer of a kit?
chunks.text:
## Q: What belongs in the trauma layer of a kit?

A: If trained: pressure bandage ("Israeli" style), hemostatic gauze, commercial tourniquet (know current protocols), chest seal, space blankets, headlamp, and trauma shears. Buy training before buying gear you do not understand. Uncontrolled bleeding and hypothermia are the field killers to plan for.

Also asked as: Israeli bandage tourniquet · hemostatic gauze kit · chest seal first aid

chunks.title: How do I treat diarrhea in a child off-grid?
chunks.text:
## Q: How do I treat diarrhea in a child off-grid?

A: 1. Offer WHO-style ORS constantly: 1 L safe water + 6 tsp sugar + ½ tsp salt.
2. Continue feeding; watch urine output and alertness.
3. Seek emergency care urgently if the child is lethargic, has bloody stool, or cannot keep fluids down — children dehydrate fastest.
Do NOT give only plain water for prolonged diarrhea without sodium/glucose, and do not wait for "it to pass" if they are worsening.

Also asked as: child dehydration ORS · kids vomiting safe water · pediatric oral rehydration

chunks.title: What over-the-counter meds are useful to store?
chunks.text:
## Q: What over-the-counter meds are useful to store?

A: Store what your household already uses: pain/fever reducers, antihistamines, anti-diarrheal, antacids — per label, rotated before expiry. The most likely medical crisis in a long disruption is running out of daily prescription medicine; discuss an emergency buffer with your doctor within the law.

Also asked as: OTC medicine preparedness · rotate home pharmacy · pain fever allergy stock

chunks.title: How do I irrigate a wound properly?
chunks.text:
## Q: How do I irrigate a wound properly?

A: Clean early: flush with copious drinkable water under pressure (an irrigation syringe helps). Remove visible debris, dress, and reassess daily. Antiseptic can help around the skin; the mechanical flush matters most. Spreading infection signs mean professional care — field care has limits.

Also asked as: wound irrigation syringe · clean cut with water · best wound cleaner field

chunks.title: What are field first-aid priorities?
chunks.text:
## Q: What are field first-aid priorities?

A: Priorities: stop severe bleeding (direct pressure first), protect airway and breathing, prevent hypothermia in any casualty, and get professional help. Carry and know your kit. Educational note only — take a certified first-aid course; hands-on practice is what works under stress.

Also asked as: wilderness first aid priorities · bleeding airway hypothermia · casualty care basics

chunks.title: How should I organise emergency food storage?
chunks.text:
## Q: How should I organise emergency food storage?

A: Use three layers: a working pantry of 2–4 weeks of what you already eat (FIFO rotation), extended storage of 3–12 months of staples (rice, oats, pasta, beans, lentils, cans, fats, salt, sugar), and deep storage of dry goods packed for years. Store cool, dark, and dry. Aim roughly 8,400 kJ (2,000 kcal) per adult per day, more for cold or heavy labour.

Also asked as: three layer pantry · how much food to store · FIFO food rotation

chunks.title: How do I pack dry goods for long-term storage?
chunks.text:
## Q: How do I pack dry goods for long-term storage?

A: Seal dry goods in Mylar bags with oxygen absorbers inside food-grade buckets. Use about 300–500 cc of absorber per 4 L of dry goods. Keep moisture ~10% or less — no brown rice, nuts, or oily goods for decades (brown rice ~6–12 months). Heat-seal, label, and date. White rice, wheat berries, beans, oats, pasta, sugar, and salt can last 20–30 years this way.

Also asked as: Mylar bags oxygen absorbers · bucket rice storage · store beans for decades

chunks.title: Why is botulism a risk with home canning?
chunks.text:
## Q: Why is botulism a risk with home canning?

A: Never taste-test a suspect can — botulism toxin is odorless. Discard bulging, leaking, or badly rusted cans. Learn pressure canning for low-acid foods (meat, broth, vegetables); a boiling-water bath is only safe for high-acid foods. Follow tested recipes exactly — improvised canning is a main modern source of botulism.

Also asked as: botulism canned food · bulging can danger · pressure canning vs water bath

chunks.title: Can I eat canned food past the best-before date?
chunks.text:
## Q: Can I eat canned food past the best-before date?

A: Canned food is often still safe well past best-before dates if cans are intact — not bulging, rusted through, or leaking. Quality declines before safety does. When in doubt, throw it out; never taste a suspect can because of botulism risk.

Also asked as: expired canned food safe · best before vs unsafe can · old tins emergency food

chunks.title: How do I cook without grid electricity?
chunks.text:
## Q: How do I cook without grid electricity?

A: Options: butane/propane camp stove (ventilate — every indoor flame makes CO), outdoor rocket stove on twigs, wood stove/fireplace with seasoned wood, solar cooker (120–180 °C on sunny days), and thermal cooking (boil then finish in heavy insulation to cut fuel use roughly in half). Cast iron and stainless survive open flame; nonstick often fails.

Also asked as: off grid cooking methods · camp stove propane rocket stove · thermal cooker fuel saving

chunks.title: Is a boiling-water bath safe for canning meat?
chunks.text:
## Q: Is a boiling-water bath safe for canning meat?

A: No. A boiling-water bath is only safe for high-acid foods (jams, pickles, tomatoes with added acid). Meat, broth, and most vegetables need a pressure canner and tested times. Improvised shortcuts risk botulism — follow tested recipes exactly.

Also asked as: water bath can meat · pressure canner required · low acid canning safety

chunks.title: How much food energy should I plan per adult per day?
chunks.text:
## Q: How much food energy should I plan per adult per day?

A: Aim about 8,400 kJ (2,000 kcal) per adult per day as a baseline, more for heavy labour and cold weather. Staples plus fats meet calories; salt and some comfort foods keep people actually eating. Children and pregnant people have different needs — plan household-specific.

Also asked as: 2000 kcal emergency · 8400 kJ per day · calorie planning storage

chunks.title: Can brown rice go in 30-year buckets?
chunks.text:
## Q: Can brown rice go in 30-year buckets?

A: No — brown rice’s oils go rancid; plan roughly 6–12 months, not decades. For multi-decade staples use white rice, wheat berries, beans, oats, pasta, sugar, and salt packed dry with oxygen absorbers (except sugar/salt/honey rules). Nuts and oily goods are short- to medium-term only.

Also asked as: brown rice storage life · why white rice stores longer · oily grains rancid

chunks.title: Why must indoor cooking flames be ventilated?
chunks.text:
## Q: Why must indoor cooking flames be ventilated?

A: Every flame indoors makes carbon monoxide. Use camp stoves with real ventilation, never as room heaters, and keep a working CO alarm. Outdoor rocket stoves and proper wood stoves with chimneys are safer patterns for fuel cooking when the grid is down.

Also asked as: camp stove indoor CO · cook inside carbon monoxide · ventilate propane burner

chunks.title: What protein foods store well without a freezer?
chunks.text:
## Q: What protein foods store well without a freezer?

A: Canned fish and meat, pressure-canned home stock, dry-cured and salted meat, hard cheeses in wax, powdered eggs and milk, plus shelf-stable fats like ghee and tallow. Learn pressure canning from tested recipes if you want low-acid home preserves — improvisation risks botulism.

Also asked as: canned fish meat storage · powdered eggs milk prep · shelf stable protein · what foods store the longest · longest storing foods · best long term foods

chunks.title: What are the ethics of hunting for food?
chunks.text:
## Q: What are the ethics of hunting for food?

A: Hunt only where licensed and legal — seasons, species, methods, and tagging rules vary. Take hunter education, learn from mentors, and make clean vital-zone shots; if not confident, do not shoot. Ethical hunting means no waste and respect for the animal. Firearms safety rules are absolute.

Also asked as: ethical hunting rules · clean kill hunting · hunt lawfully

chunks.title: How do I field dress a deer-sized animal?
chunks.text:
## Q: How do I field dress a deer-sized animal?

A: 1. Move to a clean spot, on its back, head uphill; dress promptly (within the hour; faster when warm).
2. Ring-cut and tie off the anus; open the belly with blade facing up, fingers guarding — shallow cuts only.
3. Free the diaphragm, cut windpipe/esophagus high, roll organs out; prop the cavity open and cool fast.
Legal tagging before moving the animal.
Do NOT puncture gut or bladder — that taints meat.

Also asked as: gut a deer steps · field dressing sequence · how to gut game

chunks.title: How cold should game meat stay?
chunks.text:
## Q: How cold should game meat stay?

A: Keep raw meat below 4 °C except during active work. Never leave it for hours in the 4–60 °C danger zone. Cool the carcass as fast as possible after gutting — that decides quality more than fancy cuts. Cook ground wild meat through; wild boar and bear need thorough cooking (trichinella risk).

Also asked as: meat temperature danger zone · cool venison fast · wild meat food safety

chunks.title: How do I field dress a rabbit safely?
chunks.text:
## Q: How do I field dress a rabbit safely?

A: Case-skin (hide peels like a glove), gut, and inspect the liver — spotted livers mean discard (tularemia risk). Always wear gloves handling rabbits. Birds: pluck or skin, remove crop and innards. Fish: bleed immediately, gut early, keep cold, and eat/salt/smoke/freeze the same day — fish spoil fastest.

Also asked as: skin rabbit field · tularemia rabbit liver · small game dressing

chunks.title: How can I preserve meat without a freezer?
chunks.text:
## Q: How can I preserve meat without a freezer?

A: Options: jerky (lean strips dried with airflow; modern-safe practice includes heating to 71 °C), salt curing from tested recipes, hot smoking (cooks/flavours) vs cold smoking only with proper curing, pressure canning cubed meat/stock, and rendering fat to tallow. Curing is chemistry — use tested ratios, not improvisation.

Also asked as: make jerky safely · salt cure meat · pressure can venison

chunks.title: Should I eat an animal I found dead?
chunks.text:
## Q: Should I eat an animal I found dead?

A: Do not eat animals found dead, meat that smelled wrong at gutting, or carcasses with abscesses/lesions. Use carcass disease testing where offered (e.g. CWD regions). When regulations and common sense say no, the freezer stays empty — food poisoning or worse is not a calorie win.

Also asked as: roadkill eat safe · diseased game meat · abscess wild meat

chunks.title: What shot placement is ethical for deer?
chunks.text:
## Q: What shot placement is ethical for deer?

A: The ethical standard is a broadside heart–lung shot at a distance you have practiced. If you are not confident, do not shoot. After the shot, wait before following so a wounded animal is not pushed far; then track blood sign carefully. Clean kills and full use of the meat are the standard.

Also asked as: heart lung shot deer · when not to shoot game · broadside hunting shot

chunks.title: How should I cook ground wild meat?
chunks.text:
## Q: How should I cook ground wild meat?

A: Cook ground wild meat through — grinding mixes surface bacteria throughout. Whole-muscle cuts are safer cooked less done if you accept the risk profile of your region. Wild boar and bear can carry trichinella — cook thoroughly; traditional cure-only methods are not safe for them.

Also asked as: venison burger temperature · minced game food safety · trichinella wild boar

chunks.title: How do I handle fish the same day for safety?
chunks.text:
## Q: How do I handle fish the same day for safety?

A: Bleed fish immediately, keep cold, and gut early (vent to gills, remove organs and the dark kidney line). Scale or fillet with a flexible knife. Eat, salt, smoke, or freeze the same day — fish spoil faster than red meat.

Also asked as: clean fish immediately · fish spoil fast · bleed gut fish

chunks.title: What firearm safety mindset applies to hunting?
chunks.text:
## Q: What firearm safety mindset applies to hunting?

A: Firearms safety rules are absolute: treat every gun as loaded, muzzle in a safe direction, finger off the trigger until ready, and identify the target and what is beyond it. No freezer full of meat is worth a negligent shot. Laws on transport and seasons still apply.

Also asked as: gun safety hunting · firearms rules absolute · safe gun handling field

chunks.title: How quickly should I field dress in warm weather?
chunks.text:
## Q: How quickly should I field dress in warm weather?

A: Body heat spoils meat — dress promptly within the hour, and faster in warm weather. Get the cavity open to air and ice/cool as soon as practical. Delayed gutting on a hot day is a common beginner way to ruin an otherwise good harvest.

Also asked as: warm weather gutting speed · meat spoilage heat hunt · cool carcass fast

chunks.title: Why wear gloves when handling rabbits?
chunks.text:
